developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_storage.vultr_storage_storage_lifecycle_rules_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Automated Bucket Lifecycle Rules for Expired Data Deletion (Tier-9 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_object_storage"
  not r.change.after.lifecycle_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure lifecycle_enabled for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_storage.vultr_storage_storage_tls_enforce_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce S3-Compatible TLS 1.3 Transport on Vultr Object Storage (Tier-10 • Profile K)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_object_storage"
  not r.change.after.min_tls_version
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure min_tls_version for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_storage.vultr_storage_storage_private_acl_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Disable Public Read Access on Sensitive Object Storage Clusters (Tier-10 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_object_storage"
  not r.change.after.public_access
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure public_access for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_storage.vultr_storage_storage_sse_aes256_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Server-Side AES-256 Encryption for Object Storage (Tier-10 • Profile M)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_object_storage"
  not r.change.after.server_side_encryption
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure server_side_encryption for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_storage.vultr_storage_storage_lifecycle_rules_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Automated Bucket Lifecycle Rules for Expired Data Deletion (Tier-10 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_object_storage"
  not r.change.after.lifecycle_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure lifecycle_enabled for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

package vultr.vultr_storage.vultr_storage_storage_tls_enforce_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce S3-Compatible TLS 1.3 Transport on Vultr Object Storage (Tier-11 • Profile O)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_object_storage"
  not r.change.after.min_tls_version
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure min_tls_version for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_storage.vultr_storage_storage_private_acl_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Disable Public Read Access on Sensitive Object Storage Clusters (Tier-11 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_object_storage"
  not r.change.after.public_access
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure public_access for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_storage.vultr_storage_storage_sse_aes256_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Server-Side AES-256 Encryption for Object Storage (Tier-11 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_object_storage"
  not r.change.after.server_side_encryption
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure server_side_encryption for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"

developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_iam.vultr_iam_iam_mfa_required_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) across All Vultr Subaccounts
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_user"
  not r.change.after.mfa_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure mfa_enabled for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_iam.vultr_iam_iam_api_key_least_privilege_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Restrict API Key Scopes to Read-Only for Auditing and Telemetry Tools
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_api_key"
  not r.change.after.acls
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure acls for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.

package vultr.vultr_iam.vultr_iam_iam_api_ip_whitelist_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce IP Whitelisting on Master and Subaccount API Tokens
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_api_key"
  not r.change.after.ip_whitelist
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ip_whitelist for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_iam.vultr_iam_iam_key_rotation_policy_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce 90-Day Key Rotation on All Automated Service API Credentials
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_api_key"
  not r.change.after.max_age_days
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure max_age_days for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

    end

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_iam.vultr_iam_iam_mfa_required_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) across All Vultr Subaccounts (Tier-2 • Profile E)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_user"
  not r.change.after.mfa_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure mfa_enabled for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_iam.vultr_iam_iam_api_key_least_privilege_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Restrict API Key Scopes to Read-Only for Auditing and Telemetry Tools (Tier-2 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_api_key"
  not r.change.after.acls
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure acls for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.

vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_iam.vultr_iam_iam_api_ip_whitelist_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce IP Whitelisting on Master and Subaccount API Tokens (Tier-2 • Profile G)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_api_key"
  not r.change.after.ip_whitelist
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ip_whitelist for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_iam.vultr_iam_iam_key_rotation_policy_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce 90-Day Key Rotation on All Automated Service API Credentials (Tier-2 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_api_key"
  not r.change.after.max_age_days
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure max_age_days for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_iam.vultr_iam_iam_mfa_required_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) across All Vultr Subaccounts (Tier-3 • Profile I)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_user"
  not r.change.after.mfa_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure mfa_enabled for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_iam.vultr_iam_iam_api_key_least_privilege_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Restrict API Key Scopes to Read-Only for Auditing and Telemetry Tools (Tier-3 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_api_key"
  not r.change.after.acls
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure acls for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_iam.vultr_iam_iam_api_ip_whitelist_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce IP Whitelisting on Master and Subaccount API Tokens (Tier-3 • Profile K)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_api_key"
  not r.change.after.ip_whitelist
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ip_whitelist for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_iam.vultr_iam_iam_key_rotation_policy_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce 90-Day Key Rotation on All Automated Service API Credentials (Tier-3 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_api_key"
  not r.change.after.max_age_days
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure max_age_days for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_iam.vultr_iam_iam_mfa_required_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) across All Vultr Subaccounts (Tier-4 • Profile M)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_user"
  not r.change.after.mfa_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure mfa_enabled for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_iam.vultr_iam_iam_api_key_least_privilege_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Restrict API Key Scopes to Read-Only for Auditing and Telemetry Tools (Tier-4 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_api_key"
  not r.change.after.acls
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure acls for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_iam.vultr_iam_iam_api_ip_whitelist_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce IP Whitelisting on Master and Subaccount API Tokens (Tier-4 • Profile O)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_api_key"
  not r.change.after.ip_whitelist
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ip_whitelist for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_iam.vultr_iam_iam_key_rotation_policy_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce 90-Day Key Rotation on All Automated Service API Credentials (Tier-4 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_api_key"
  not r.change.after.max_age_days
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure max_age_days for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_iam.vultr_iam_iam_mfa_required_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) across All Vultr Subaccounts (Tier-5 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_user"
  not r.change.after.mfa_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure mfa_enabled for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.

vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_iam.vultr_iam_iam_api_key_least_privilege_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Restrict API Key Scopes to Read-Only for Auditing and Telemetry Tools (Tier-5 • Profile R)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_api_key"
  not r.change.after.acls
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure acls for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.

vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_iam.vultr_iam_iam_api_ip_whitelist_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce IP Whitelisting on Master and Subaccount API Tokens (Tier-5 • Profile S)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_api_key"
  not r.change.after.ip_whitelist
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ip_whitelist for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_iam.vultr_iam_iam_key_rotation_policy_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce 90-Day Key Rotation on All Automated Service API Credentials (Tier-5 • Profile T)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_api_key"
  not r.change.after.max_age_days
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure max_age_days for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_iam.vultr_iam_iam_mfa_required_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) across All Vultr Subaccounts (Tier-6 • Profile U)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_user"
  not r.change.after.mfa_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure mfa_enabled for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_iam.vultr_iam_iam_api_key_least_privilege_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Restrict API Key Scopes to Read-Only for Auditing and Telemetry Tools (Tier-6 • Profile V)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_api_key"
  not r.change.after.acls
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure acls for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_iam.vultr_iam_iam_api_ip_whitelist_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce IP Whitelisting on Master and Subaccount API Tokens (Tier-6 • Profile W)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_api_key"
  not r.change.after.ip_whitelist
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ip_whitelist for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_iam.vultr_iam_iam_key_rotation_policy_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce 90-Day Key Rotation on All Automated Service API Credentials (Tier-6 • Profile X)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_api_key"
  not r.change.after.max_age_days
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure max_age_days for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_iam.vultr_iam_iam_mfa_required_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) across All Vultr Subaccounts (Tier-7 • Profile Y)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_user"
  not r.change.after.mfa_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure mfa_enabled for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_iam.vultr_iam_iam_api_key_least_privilege_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Restrict API Key Scopes to Read-Only for Auditing and Telemetry Tools (Tier-7 • Profile Z)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_api_key"
  not r.change.after.acls
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure acls for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_iam.vultr_iam_iam_api_ip_whitelist_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce IP Whitelisting on Master and Subaccount API Tokens (Tier-7 • Profile A)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_api_key"
  not r.change.after.ip_whitelist
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ip_whitelist for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_iam.vultr_iam_iam_key_rotation_policy_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce 90-Day Key Rotation on All Automated Service API Credentials (Tier-7 • Profile B)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_api_key"
  not r.change.after.max_age_days
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure max_age_days for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
