developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_instance.vultr_instance_instance_firewall_group_attached_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Attach Managed Cloud Firewall Group on Compute Instance Launch (Tier-3 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.firewall_group_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure firewall_group_id for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_instance.vultr_instance_instance_auto_backup_enabled_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Automated Daily OS Snapshots on All Production Instances (Tier-3 • Profile K)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Cloud Compute"]
      requirement["Enable Automated Daily OS Snapshots on All Production Instances"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0140"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-instance", label: "Vultr Cloud Compute", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_instance.vultr_instance_instance_ddos_protection_enabled_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable DDoS Protection on All Public Facing Compute Instances (Tier-3 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.ddos_protection
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ddos_protection for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_instance.vultr_instance_instance_ssh_key_only_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce SSH Key-Based Authentication and Disable Password Logins (Tier-4 • Profile M)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.ssh_key_ids
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ssh_key_ids for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_instance.vultr_instance_instance_firewall_group_attached_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Attach Managed Cloud Firewall Group on Compute Instance Launch (Tier-4 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.firewall_group_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure firewall_group_id for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Cloud Compute"]
      requirement["Attach Managed Cloud Firewall Group on Compute Instance Launch"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0143"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-instance", label: "Vultr Cloud Compute", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_instance.vultr_instance_instance_auto_backup_enabled_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Automated Daily OS Snapshots on All Production Instances (Tier-4 • Profile O)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_instance.vultr_instance_instance_ddos_protection_enabled_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable DDoS Protection on All Public Facing Compute Instances (Tier-4 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.ddos_protection
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ddos_protection for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_instance.vultr_instance_instance_ssh_key_only_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce SSH Key-Based Authentication and Disable Password Logins (Tier-5 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.ssh_key_ids
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ssh_key_ids for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Cloud Compute"]
      requirement["Enforce SSH Key-Based Authentication and Disable Password Logins"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0146"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-instance", label: "Vultr Cloud Compute", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_instance.vultr_instance_instance_firewall_group_attached_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Attach Managed Cloud Firewall Group on Compute Instance Launch (Tier-5 • Profile R)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.firewall_group_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure firewall_group_id for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_instance.vultr_instance_instance_auto_backup_enabled_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Automated Daily OS Snapshots on All Production Instances (Tier-5 • Profile S)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Cloud Compute"]
      requirement["Enable Automated Daily OS Snapshots on All Production Instances"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0148"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-instance", label: "Vultr Cloud Compute", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.

checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_instance.vultr_instance_instance_ddos_protection_enabled_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable DDoS Protection on All Public Facing Compute Instances (Tier-5 • Profile T)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.ddos_protection
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ddos_protection for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_instance.vultr_instance_instance_ssh_key_only_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce SSH Key-Based Authentication and Disable Password Logins (Tier-6 • Profile U)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.ssh_key_ids
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ssh_key_ids for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_instance.vultr_instance_instance_firewall_group_attached_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Attach Managed Cloud Firewall Group on Compute Instance Launch (Tier-6 • Profile V)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.firewall_group_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure firewall_group_id for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Cloud Compute"]
      requirement["Attach Managed Cloud Firewall Group on Compute Instance Launch"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0151"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-instance", label: "Vultr Cloud Compute", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_instance.vultr_instance_instance_auto_backup_enabled_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Automated Daily OS Snapshots on All Production Instances (Tier-6 • Profile W)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_instance.vultr_instance_instance_ddos_protection_enabled_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable DDoS Protection on All Public Facing Compute Instances (Tier-6 • Profile X)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.ddos_protection
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ddos_protection for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome

      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_instance.vultr_instance_instance_ssh_key_only_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce SSH Key-Based Authentication and Disable Password Logins (Tier-7 • Profile Y)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.ssh_key_ids
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ssh_key_ids for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Cloud Compute"]
      requirement["Enforce SSH Key-Based Authentication and Disable Password Logins"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0154"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-instance", label: "Vultr Cloud Compute", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_instance.vultr_instance_instance_firewall_group_attached_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Attach Managed Cloud Firewall Group on Compute Instance Launch (Tier-7 • Profile Z)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.firewall_group_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure firewall_group_id for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_instance.vultr_instance_instance_auto_backup_enabled_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Automated Daily OS Snapshots on All Production Instances (Tier-7 • Profile A)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Cloud Compute"]
      requirement["Enable Automated Daily OS Snapshots on All Production Instances"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0156"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-instance", label: "Vultr Cloud Compute", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_instance.vultr_instance_instance_ddos_protection_enabled_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable DDoS Protection on All Public Facing Compute Instances (Tier-7 • Profile B)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.ddos_protection
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ddos_protection for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_instance.vultr_instance_instance_ssh_key_only_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce SSH Key-Based Authentication and Disable Password Logins (Tier-8 • Profile C)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.ssh_key_ids
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ssh_key_ids for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_instance.vultr_instance_instance_firewall_group_attached_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Attach Managed Cloud Firewall Group on Compute Instance Launch (Tier-8 • Profile D)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.firewall_group_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure firewall_group_id for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Cloud Compute"]
      requirement["Attach Managed Cloud Firewall Group on Compute Instance Launch"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0159"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-instance", label: "Vultr Cloud Compute", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_instance.vultr_instance_instance_auto_backup_enabled_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Automated Daily OS Snapshots on All Production Instances (Tier-8 • Profile E)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable DDoS Protection on All Public Facing Compute Instances (Tier-8 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.ddos_protection
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ddos_protection for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_instance.vultr_instance_instance_ssh_key_only_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce SSH Key-Based Authentication and Disable Password Logins (Tier-9 • Profile G)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.ssh_key_ids
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ssh_key_ids for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Cloud Compute"]
      requirement["Enforce SSH Key-Based Authentication and Disable Password Logins"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0162"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-instance", label: "Vultr Cloud Compute", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_instance.vultr_instance_instance_firewall_group_attached_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Attach Managed Cloud Firewall Group on Compute Instance Launch (Tier-9 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.firewall_group_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure firewall_group_id for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_instance.vultr_instance_instance_auto_backup_enabled_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Automated Daily OS Snapshots on All Production Instances (Tier-9 • Profile I)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Cloud Compute"]
      requirement["Enable Automated Daily OS Snapshots on All Production Instances"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0164"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-instance", label: "Vultr Cloud Compute", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_instance.vultr_instance_instance_ddos_protection_enabled_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable DDoS Protection on All Public Facing Compute Instances (Tier-9 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.ddos_protection
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ddos_protection for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_instance.vultr_instance_instance_ssh_key_only_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce SSH Key-Based Authentication and Disable Password Logins (Tier-10 • Profile K)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.ssh_key_ids
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ssh_key_ids for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
