developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_instance.vultr_instance_instance_firewall_group_attached_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Attach Managed Cloud Firewall Group on Compute Instance Launch (Tier-10 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.firewall_group_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure firewall_group_id for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Cloud Compute"]
      requirement["Attach Managed Cloud Firewall Group on Compute Instance Launch"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0167"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-instance", label: "Vultr Cloud Compute", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.

vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_instance.vultr_instance_instance_auto_backup_enabled_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Automated Daily OS Snapshots on All Production Instances (Tier-10 • Profile M)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable DDoS Protection on All Public Facing Compute Instances (Tier-10 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.ddos_protection
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ddos_protection for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_instance.vultr_instance_instance_ssh_key_only_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce SSH Key-Based Authentication and Disable Password Logins (Tier-11 • Profile O)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.ssh_key_ids
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ssh_key_ids for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Cloud Compute"]
      requirement["Enforce SSH Key-Based Authentication and Disable Password Logins"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0170"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-instance", label: "Vultr Cloud Compute", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_instance.vultr_instance_instance_firewall_group_attached_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Attach Managed Cloud Firewall Group on Compute Instance Launch (Tier-11 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.firewall_group_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure firewall_group_id for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_instance.vultr_instance_instance_auto_backup_enabled_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Automated Daily OS Snapshots on All Production Instances (Tier-11 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Cloud Compute"]
      requirement["Enable Automated Daily OS Snapshots on All Production Instances"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0172"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-instance", label: "Vultr Cloud Compute", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.

tests: Call the health route and a real application route.

failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_ip_whitelist_enforced_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Trusted IP Whitelists on Managed Database Access Control
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.trusted_ips
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure trusted_ips for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_require_tls_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce TLS 1.3 Transport Encryption for Client Database Connections
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.require_ssl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure require_ssl for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_pitr_enabled_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Automated Point-in-Time Recovery and Daily Backups
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.backup_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backup_enabled for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Databases"]
      requirement["Enable Automated Point-in-Time Recovery and Daily Backups"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0175"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-database", label: "Vultr Managed Databases", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.

vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_ha_cluster_nodes_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Managed Database in High-Availability Multi-Node Cluster
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.plan_replicas
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure plan_replicas for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_ip_whitelist_enforced_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Trusted IP Whitelists on Managed Database Access Control (Tier-2 • Profile E)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.trusted_ips
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure trusted_ips for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Databases"]
      requirement["Enforce Trusted IP Whitelists on Managed Database Access Control"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0177"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-database", label: "Vultr Managed Databases", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_require_tls_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce TLS 1.3 Transport Encryption for Client Database Connections (Tier-2 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.require_ssl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure require_ssl for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_pitr_enabled_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Automated Point-in-Time Recovery and Daily Backups (Tier-2 • Profile G)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.backup_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backup_enabled for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Databases"]
      requirement["Enable Automated Point-in-Time Recovery and Daily Backups"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0179"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-database", label: "Vultr Managed Databases", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool

tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.

failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.

package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_ha_cluster_nodes_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Managed Database in High-Availability Multi-Node Cluster (Tier-2 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.plan_replicas
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure plan_replicas for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_ip_whitelist_enforced_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Trusted IP Whitelists on Managed Database Access Control (Tier-3 • Profile I)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.trusted_ips
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure trusted_ips for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}

tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.

Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_require_tls_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce TLS 1.3 Transport Encryption for Client Database Connections (Tier-3 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.require_ssl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure require_ssl for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Databases"]
      requirement["Enforce TLS 1.3 Transport Encryption for Client Database Connections"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0182"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-database", label: "Vultr Managed Databases", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_pitr_enabled_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Automated Point-in-Time Recovery and Daily Backups (Tier-3 • Profile K)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.backup_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backup_enabled for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_ha_cluster_nodes_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Managed Database in High-Availability Multi-Node Cluster (Tier-3 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.plan_replicas
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure plan_replicas for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Databases"]
      requirement["Deploy Managed Database in High-Availability Multi-Node Cluster"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0184"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-database", label: "Vultr Managed Databases", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool

tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.

failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.

package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_ip_whitelist_enforced_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Trusted IP Whitelists on Managed Database Access Control (Tier-4 • Profile M)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.trusted_ips
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure trusted_ips for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.

vultr-cli instance list

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_require_tls_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce TLS 1.3 Transport Encryption for Client Database Connections (Tier-4 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.require_ssl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure require_ssl for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Databases"]
      requirement["Enforce TLS 1.3 Transport Encryption for Client Database Connections"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0186"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-database", label: "Vultr Managed Databases", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_pitr_enabled_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Automated Point-in-Time Recovery and Daily Backups (Tier-4 • Profile O)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.backup_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backup_enabled for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

# Rule: Deploy Managed Database in High-Availability Multi-Node Cluster (Tier-4 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.plan_replicas
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure plan_replicas for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_ip_whitelist_enforced_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Trusted IP Whitelists on Managed Database Access Control (Tier-5 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.trusted_ips
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure trusted_ips for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Databases"]
      requirement["Enforce Trusted IP Whitelists on Managed Database Access Control"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0189"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-database", label: "Vultr Managed Databases", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_require_tls_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce TLS 1.3 Transport Encryption for Client Database Connections (Tier-5 • Profile R)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.require_ssl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure require_ssl for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_pitr_enabled_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Automated Point-in-Time Recovery and Daily Backups (Tier-5 • Profile S)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.backup_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backup_enabled for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Databases"]
      requirement["Enable Automated Point-in-Time Recovery and Daily Backups"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0191"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-database", label: "Vultr Managed Databases", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.

package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_ha_cluster_nodes_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Managed Database in High-Availability Multi-Node Cluster (Tier-5 • Profile T)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.plan_replicas
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure plan_replicas for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_ip_whitelist_enforced_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Trusted IP Whitelists on Managed Database Access Control (Tier-6 • Profile U)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.trusted_ips
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure trusted_ips for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Databases"]
      requirement["Enforce Trusted IP Whitelists on Managed Database Access Control"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0193"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-database", label: "Vultr Managed Databases", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_require_tls_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce TLS 1.3 Transport Encryption for Client Database Connections (Tier-6 • Profile V)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.require_ssl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure require_ssl for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_pitr_enabled_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Automated Point-in-Time Recovery and Daily Backups (Tier-6 • Profile W)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.backup_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backup_enabled for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.

vultr-cli account info

vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets

package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_ha_cluster_nodes_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Managed Database in High-Availability Multi-Node Cluster (Tier-6 • Profile X)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.plan_replicas
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure plan_replicas for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.

: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_ip_whitelist_enforced_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Trusted IP Whitelists on Managed Database Access Control (Tier-7 • Profile Y)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.trusted_ips
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure trusted_ips for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_require_tls_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce TLS 1.3 Transport Encryption for Client Database Connections (Tier-7 • Profile Z)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.require_ssl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure require_ssl for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Databases"]
      requirement["Enforce TLS 1.3 Transport Encryption for Client Database Connections"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0198"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-database", label: "Vultr Managed Databases", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end
