developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.

checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_pitr_enabled_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Automated Point-in-Time Recovery and Daily Backups (Tier-7 • Profile A)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.backup_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backup_enabled for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_ha_cluster_nodes_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Managed Database in High-Availability Multi-Node Cluster (Tier-7 • Profile B)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.plan_replicas
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure plan_replicas for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Databases"]
      requirement["Deploy Managed Database in High-Availability Multi-Node Cluster"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0200"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-database", label: "Vultr Managed Databases", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.

package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_ip_whitelist_enforced_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Trusted IP Whitelists on Managed Database Access Control (Tier-8 • Profile C)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.trusted_ips
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure trusted_ips for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.

vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_require_tls_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce TLS 1.3 Transport Encryption for Client Database Connections (Tier-8 • Profile D)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.require_ssl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure require_ssl for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0202"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-database", label: "Vultr Managed Databases", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.

package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_pitr_enabled_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Automated Point-in-Time Recovery and Daily Backups (Tier-8 • Profile E)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.backup_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backup_enabled for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_ha_cluster_nodes_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Managed Database in High-Availability Multi-Node Cluster (Tier-8 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.plan_replicas
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure plan_replicas for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_ip_whitelist_enforced_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Trusted IP Whitelists on Managed Database Access Control (Tier-9 • Profile G)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.trusted_ips
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure trusted_ips for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Databases"]
      requirement["Enforce Trusted IP Whitelists on Managed Database Access Control"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0205"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-database", label: "Vultr Managed Databases", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_require_tls_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce TLS 1.3 Transport Encryption for Client Database Connections (Tier-9 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.require_ssl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure require_ssl for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_pitr_enabled_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Automated Point-in-Time Recovery and Daily Backups (Tier-9 • Profile I)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.backup_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backup_enabled for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Databases"]
      requirement["Enable Automated Point-in-Time Recovery and Daily Backups"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0207"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-database", label: "Vultr Managed Databases", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.

package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_ha_cluster_nodes_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Managed Database in High-Availability Multi-Node Cluster (Tier-9 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.plan_replicas
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure plan_replicas for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_ip_whitelist_enforced_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Trusted IP Whitelists on Managed Database Access Control (Tier-10 • Profile K)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.trusted_ips
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure trusted_ips for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Databases"]

      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0209"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-database", label: "Vultr Managed Databases", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_require_tls_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce TLS 1.3 Transport Encryption for Client Database Connections (Tier-10 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.require_ssl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure require_ssl for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_pitr_enabled_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Automated Point-in-Time Recovery and Daily Backups (Tier-10 • Profile M)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.backup_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backup_enabled for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_ha_cluster_nodes_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Managed Database in High-Availability Multi-Node Cluster (Tier-10 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.plan_replicas
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure plan_replicas for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Databases"]
      requirement["Deploy Managed Database in High-Availability Multi-Node Cluster"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0212"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-database", label: "Vultr Managed Databases", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics

Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.

Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.

package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_ip_whitelist_enforced_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Trusted IP Whitelists on Managed Database Access Control (Tier-11 • Profile O)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.trusted_ips
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure trusted_ips for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.

vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_require_tls_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce TLS 1.3 Transport Encryption for Client Database Connections (Tier-11 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.require_ssl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure require_ssl for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Databases"]
      requirement["Enforce TLS 1.3 Transport Encryption for Client Database Connections"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0214"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-database", label: "Vultr Managed Databases", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_database.vultr_database_database_pitr_enabled_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Automated Point-in-Time Recovery and Daily Backups (Tier-11 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.backup_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backup_enabled for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_kubernetes.vultr_kubernetes_vke_private_nodes_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy VKE Worker Nodes Exclusively in Private VPC Networks
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_kubernetes"
  not r.change.after.node_pools
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure node_pools.vpc2_id for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Kubernetes Engine"]
      requirement["Deploy VKE Worker Nodes Exclusively in Private VPC Networks"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0216"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-kubernetes", label: "Vultr Kubernetes Engine", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Container application on a managed Kubernetes cluster
developer_guide.contract: Service port, Pod targetPort, readiness path and immutable image digest
dependencies: A reachable cluster API and an image registry
A namespace, workload identity and network policy capable CNI
An ingress or gateway controller when external access is required
steps: Push an image by immutable digest and grant registry pull access.
Apply Deployment, Service and any ingress configuration.
Verify endpoints and readiness before exposing traffic.
tests: Check rollout status and populated Service endpoints.
Remove a replica and verify normal requests continue.
Exercise the configured ingress and egress denial paths.
failures: ImagePullBackOff: inspect registry identity and image digest.
Service timeout: inspect selectors, readiness, targetPort and CNI rules.

vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_kubernetes.vultr_kubernetes_vke_psa_admission_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Kubernetes Admission Controllers for Pod Security Standards
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_kubernetes"
  not r.change.after.pod_security_standard
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure pod_security_standard for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted

developer_guide.name: Container application on a managed Kubernetes cluster
developer_guide.contract: Service port, Pod targetPort, readiness path and immutable image digest
dependencies: A reachable cluster API and an image registry
A namespace, workload identity and network policy capable CNI
An ingress or gateway controller when external access is required
steps: Push an image by immutable digest and grant registry pull access.
Apply Deployment, Service and any ingress configuration.
Verify endpoints and readiness before exposing traffic.
tests: Check rollout status and populated Service endpoints.
Remove a replica and verify normal requests continue.
Exercise the configured ingress and egress denial paths.
failures: ImagePullBackOff: inspect registry identity and image digest.
Service timeout: inspect selectors, readiness, targetPort and CNI rules.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_kubernetes.vultr_kubernetes_vke_auto_upgrade_patch_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Auto-Upgrade Policies for VKE Control Plane and Worker Pools
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_kubernetes"
  not r.change.after.auto_upgrade
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure auto_upgrade for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Container application on a managed Kubernetes cluster
developer_guide.contract: Service port, Pod targetPort, readiness path and immutable image digest
dependencies: A reachable cluster API and an image registry
A namespace, workload identity and network policy capable CNI
An ingress or gateway controller when external access is required
steps: Push an image by immutable digest and grant registry pull access.
Apply Deployment, Service and any ingress configuration.
Verify endpoints and readiness before exposing traffic.
tests: Check rollout status and populated Service endpoints.
Remove a replica and verify normal requests continue.
Exercise the configured ingress and egress denial paths.
failures: ImagePullBackOff: inspect registry identity and image digest.
Service timeout: inspect selectors, readiness, targetPort and CNI rules.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_kubernetes.vultr_kubernetes_vke_ingress_firewall_rules_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Cloud Firewall Rules on VKE Ingress Node Ports
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_group"
  not r.change.after.description
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure description for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Kubernetes Engine"]
      requirement["Enforce Cloud Firewall Rules on VKE Ingress Node Ports"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0219"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-kubernetes", label: "Vultr Kubernetes Engine", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Container application on a managed Kubernetes cluster
developer_guide.contract: Service port, Pod targetPort, readiness path and immutable image digest
dependencies: A reachable cluster API and an image registry
A namespace, workload identity and network policy capable CNI
An ingress or gateway controller when external access is required
steps: Push an image by immutable digest and grant registry pull access.
Apply Deployment, Service and any ingress configuration.
Verify endpoints and readiness before exposing traffic.
tests: Check rollout status and populated Service endpoints.
Remove a replica and verify normal requests continue.
Exercise the configured ingress and egress denial paths.
failures: ImagePullBackOff: inspect registry identity and image digest.
Service timeout: inspect selectors, readiness, targetPort and CNI rules.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_kubernetes.vultr_kubernetes_vke_private_nodes_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy VKE Worker Nodes Exclusively in Private VPC Networks (Tier-2 • Profile E)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_kubernetes"
  not r.change.after.node_pools
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure node_pools.vpc2_id for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Kubernetes Engine"]
      requirement["Deploy VKE Worker Nodes Exclusively in Private VPC Networks"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]

developer_guide.name: Container application on a managed Kubernetes cluster
developer_guide.contract: Service port, Pod targetPort, readiness path and immutable image digest
dependencies: A reachable cluster API and an image registry
A namespace, workload identity and network policy capable CNI
An ingress or gateway controller when external access is required
steps: Push an image by immutable digest and grant registry pull access.
Apply Deployment, Service and any ingress configuration.
Verify endpoints and readiness before exposing traffic.
tests: Check rollout status and populated Service endpoints.
Remove a replica and verify normal requests continue.
Exercise the configured ingress and egress denial paths.
failures: ImagePullBackOff: inspect registry identity and image digest.
Service timeout: inspect selectors, readiness, targetPort and CNI rules.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_kubernetes.vultr_kubernetes_vke_psa_admission_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Kubernetes Admission Controllers for Pod Security Standards (Tier-2 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_kubernetes"
  not r.change.after.pod_security_standard
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure pod_security_standard for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Kubernetes Engine"]
      requirement["Enable Kubernetes Admission Controllers for Pod Security Standards"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0221"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-kubernetes", label: "Vultr Kubernetes Engine", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Container application on a managed Kubernetes cluster
developer_guide.contract: Service port, Pod targetPort, readiness path and immutable image digest
dependencies: A reachable cluster API and an image registry
A namespace, workload identity and network policy capable CNI
An ingress or gateway controller when external access is required
steps: Push an image by immutable digest and grant registry pull access.
Apply Deployment, Service and any ingress configuration.
Verify endpoints and readiness before exposing traffic.
tests: Check rollout status and populated Service endpoints.
Remove a replica and verify normal requests continue.
Exercise the configured ingress and egress denial paths.
failures: ImagePullBackOff: inspect registry identity and image digest.
Service timeout: inspect selectors, readiness, targetPort and CNI rules.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_kubernetes.vultr_kubernetes_vke_auto_upgrade_patch_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Auto-Upgrade Policies for VKE Control Plane and Worker Pools (Tier-2 • Profile G)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_kubernetes"
  not r.change.after.auto_upgrade
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure auto_upgrade for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Container application on a managed Kubernetes cluster
developer_guide.contract: Service port, Pod targetPort, readiness path and immutable image digest
dependencies: A reachable cluster API and an image registry
A namespace, workload identity and network policy capable CNI
An ingress or gateway controller when external access is required
steps: Push an image by immutable digest and grant registry pull access.
Apply Deployment, Service and any ingress configuration.
Verify endpoints and readiness before exposing traffic.
tests: Check rollout status and populated Service endpoints.
Remove a replica and verify normal requests continue.
Exercise the configured ingress and egress denial paths.
failures: ImagePullBackOff: inspect registry identity and image digest.
Service timeout: inspect selectors, readiness, targetPort and CNI rules.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_kubernetes.vultr_kubernetes_vke_ingress_firewall_rules_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Cloud Firewall Rules on VKE Ingress Node Ports (Tier-2 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_group"
  not r.change.after.description
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure description for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Kubernetes Engine"]
      requirement["Enforce Cloud Firewall Rules on VKE Ingress Node Ports"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0223"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-kubernetes", label: "Vultr Kubernetes Engine", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Container application on a managed Kubernetes cluster
developer_guide.contract: Service port, Pod targetPort, readiness path and immutable image digest
dependencies: A reachable cluster API and an image registry
A namespace, workload identity and network policy capable CNI
An ingress or gateway controller when external access is required
steps: Push an image by immutable digest and grant registry pull access.
Apply Deployment, Service and any ingress configuration.
Verify endpoints and readiness before exposing traffic.
tests: Check rollout status and populated Service endpoints.
Remove a replica and verify normal requests continue.
Exercise the configured ingress and egress denial paths.
failures: ImagePullBackOff: inspect registry identity and image digest.
Service timeout: inspect selectors, readiness, targetPort and CNI rules.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_kubernetes.vultr_kubernetes_vke_private_nodes_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy VKE Worker Nodes Exclusively in Private VPC Networks (Tier-3 • Profile I)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_kubernetes"
  not r.change.after.node_pools
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure node_pools.vpc2_id for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Container application on a managed Kubernetes cluster
developer_guide.contract: Service port, Pod targetPort, readiness path and immutable image digest
dependencies: A reachable cluster API and an image registry
A namespace, workload identity and network policy capable CNI
An ingress or gateway controller when external access is required
steps: Push an image by immutable digest and grant registry pull access.
Apply Deployment, Service and any ingress configuration.
Verify endpoints and readiness before exposing traffic.
tests: Check rollout status and populated Service endpoints.
Remove a replica and verify normal requests continue.
Exercise the configured ingress and egress denial paths.
failures: ImagePullBackOff: inspect registry identity and image digest.
Service timeout: inspect selectors, readiness, targetPort and CNI rules.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_kubernetes.vultr_kubernetes_vke_psa_admission_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Kubernetes Admission Controllers for Pod Security Standards (Tier-3 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_kubernetes"
  not r.change.after.pod_security_standard
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure pod_security_standard for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Kubernetes Engine"]
      requirement["Enable Kubernetes Admission Controllers for Pod Security Standards"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0225"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-kubernetes", label: "Vultr Kubernetes Engine", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Container application on a managed Kubernetes cluster
developer_guide.contract: Service port, Pod targetPort, readiness path and immutable image digest
dependencies: A reachable cluster API and an image registry
A namespace, workload identity and network policy capable CNI
An ingress or gateway controller when external access is required
steps: Push an image by immutable digest and grant registry pull access.
Apply Deployment, Service and any ingress configuration.
Verify endpoints and readiness before exposing traffic.
tests: Check rollout status and populated Service endpoints.
Remove a replica and verify normal requests continue.
Exercise the configured ingress and egress denial paths.
failures: ImagePullBackOff: inspect registry identity and image digest.
Service timeout: inspect selectors, readiness, targetPort and CNI rules.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_kubernetes.vultr_kubernetes_vke_auto_upgrade_patch_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Auto-Upgrade Policies for VKE Control Plane and Worker Pools (Tier-3 • Profile K)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_kubernetes"
  not r.change.after.auto_upgrade
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure auto_upgrade for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Container application on a managed Kubernetes cluster
developer_guide.contract: Service port, Pod targetPort, readiness path and immutable image digest
dependencies: A reachable cluster API and an image registry
A namespace, workload identity and network policy capable CNI
An ingress or gateway controller when external access is required
steps: Push an image by immutable digest and grant registry pull access.
Apply Deployment, Service and any ingress configuration.
Verify endpoints and readiness before exposing traffic.
tests: Check rollout status and populated Service endpoints.
Remove a replica and verify normal requests continue.
Exercise the configured ingress and egress denial paths.
failures: ImagePullBackOff: inspect registry identity and image digest.
Service timeout: inspect selectors, readiness, targetPort and CNI rules.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_kubernetes.vultr_kubernetes_vke_ingress_firewall_rules_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Cloud Firewall Rules on VKE Ingress Node Ports (Tier-3 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_group"
  not r.change.after.description
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure description for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Kubernetes Engine"]
      requirement["Enforce Cloud Firewall Rules on VKE Ingress Node Ports"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0227"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-kubernetes", label: "Vultr Kubernetes Engine", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end
