developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_firewall.vultr_firewall_firewall_deny_plaintext_http_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Block Plaintext HTTP Port 80 Ingress and Enforce TLS Port 443 (Tier-7 • Profile A)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_rule"
  not r.change.after.port
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure port for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_firewall.vultr_firewall_firewall_group_all_subnets_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Centralized Cloud Firewall Across All VPC Instance Subnets (Tier-7 • Profile B)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_group"
  not r.change.after.subnet_attachment
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure subnet_attachment for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.

package vultr.vultr_firewall.vultr_firewall_firewall_default_deny_ingress_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Default-Deny Ingress Rule Set on Vultr Firewall Groups (Tier-8 • Profile C)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_group"
  not r.change.after.default_ingress
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure default_ingress for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.

package vultr.vultr_firewall.vultr_firewall_firewall_restrict_ssh_cidr_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Restrict SSH Port 22 Ingress to Authorized Administrative Bastion CIDRs (Tier-8 • Profile D)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_rule"
  not r.change.after.port
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure port for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_firewall.vultr_firewall_firewall_deny_plaintext_http_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Block Plaintext HTTP Port 80 Ingress and Enforce TLS Port 443 (Tier-8 • Profile E)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_rule"
  not r.change.after.port
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure port for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_firewall.vultr_firewall_firewall_group_all_subnets_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Centralized Cloud Firewall Across All VPC Instance Subnets (Tier-8 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_group"
  not r.change.after.subnet_attachment
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure subnet_attachment for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Firewall"]
      requirement["Deploy Centralized Cloud Firewall Across All VPC Instance Subnets"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0290"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-firewall", label: "Vultr Firewall", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.

package vultr.vultr_firewall.vultr_firewall_firewall_default_deny_ingress_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Default-Deny Ingress Rule Set on Vultr Firewall Groups (Tier-9 • Profile G)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_group"
  not r.change.after.default_ingress
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure default_ingress for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_firewall.vultr_firewall_firewall_restrict_ssh_cidr_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Restrict SSH Port 22 Ingress to Authorized Administrative Bastion CIDRs (Tier-9 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_rule"
  not r.change.after.port
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure port for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_firewall.vultr_firewall_firewall_deny_plaintext_http_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Block Plaintext HTTP Port 80 Ingress and Enforce TLS Port 443 (Tier-9 • Profile I)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_rule"
  not r.change.after.port
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure port for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_firewall.vultr_firewall_firewall_group_all_subnets_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Centralized Cloud Firewall Across All VPC Instance Subnets (Tier-9 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_group"
  not r.change.after.subnet_attachment
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure subnet_attachment for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0294"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-firewall", label: "Vultr Firewall", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.

package vultr.vultr_firewall.vultr_firewall_firewall_default_deny_ingress_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Default-Deny Ingress Rule Set on Vultr Firewall Groups (Tier-10 • Profile K)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_group"
  not r.change.after.default_ingress
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure default_ingress for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_firewall.vultr_firewall_firewall_restrict_ssh_cidr_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Restrict SSH Port 22 Ingress to Authorized Administrative Bastion CIDRs (Tier-10 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_rule"
  not r.change.after.port
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure port for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_firewall.vultr_firewall_firewall_deny_plaintext_http_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Block Plaintext HTTP Port 80 Ingress and Enforce TLS Port 443 (Tier-10 • Profile M)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_rule"
  not r.change.after.port
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure port for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Firewall"]
      requirement["Block Plaintext HTTP Port 80 Ingress and Enforce TLS Port 443"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0297"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-firewall", label: "Vultr Firewall", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.

vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_firewall.vultr_firewall_firewall_group_all_subnets_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Centralized Cloud Firewall Across All VPC Instance Subnets (Tier-10 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_group"
  not r.change.after.subnet_attachment
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure subnet_attachment for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_firewall.vultr_firewall_firewall_default_deny_ingress_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Default-Deny Ingress Rule Set on Vultr Firewall Groups (Tier-11 • Profile O)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_group"
  not r.change.after.default_ingress
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure default_ingress for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_firewall.vultr_firewall_firewall_restrict_ssh_cidr_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Restrict SSH Port 22 Ingress to Authorized Administrative Bastion CIDRs (Tier-11 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_rule"
  not r.change.after.port
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure port for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.

package vultr.vultr_firewall.vultr_firewall_firewall_deny_plaintext_http_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Block Plaintext HTTP Port 80 Ingress and Enforce TLS Port 443 (Tier-11 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_rule"
  not r.change.after.port
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure port for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.

developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_ssl_modern_ciphers_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Modern TLS 1.3 Cyphers on Vultr Load Balancer SSL Termination
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.ssl_redirect
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ssl_redirect for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_hsts_header_enabled_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) on Load Balancer Listeners
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.hsts_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure hsts_enabled for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_health_checks_strict_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Strict TCP and HTTP Health Checks for Backend Nodes
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.health_check
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure health_check.check_interval for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_access_logs_archived_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Access Logging to Vultr Object Storage for Request Auditing
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.logging_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure logging_enabled for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_ssl_modern_ciphers_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Modern TLS 1.3 Cyphers on Vultr Load Balancer SSL Termination (Tier-2 • Profile E)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.ssl_redirect
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ssl_redirect for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_hsts_header_enabled_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) on Load Balancer Listeners (Tier-2 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.hsts_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure hsts_enabled for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_health_checks_strict_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Strict TCP and HTTP Health Checks for Backend Nodes (Tier-2 • Profile G)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.health_check
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure health_check.check_interval for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Load Balancer"]
      requirement["Configure Strict TCP and HTTP Health Checks for Backend Nodes"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0308"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-loadbalancer", label: "Vultr Load Balancer", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_access_logs_archived_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Access Logging to Vultr Object Storage for Request Auditing (Tier-2 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.logging_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure logging_enabled for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_ssl_modern_ciphers_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Modern TLS 1.3 Cyphers on Vultr Load Balancer SSL Termination (Tier-3 • Profile I)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.ssl_redirect
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ssl_redirect for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_hsts_header_enabled_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) on Load Balancer Listeners (Tier-3 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.hsts_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure hsts_enabled for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_health_checks_strict_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Strict TCP and HTTP Health Checks for Backend Nodes (Tier-3 • Profile K)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.health_check
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure health_check.check_interval for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Load Balancer"]
      requirement["Configure Strict TCP and HTTP Health Checks for Backend Nodes"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0312"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-loadbalancer", label: "Vultr Load Balancer", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_access_logs_archived_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Access Logging to Vultr Object Storage for Request Auditing (Tier-3 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.logging_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure logging_enabled for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_ssl_modern_ciphers_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Modern TLS 1.3 Cyphers on Vultr Load Balancer SSL Termination (Tier-4 • Profile M)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.ssl_redirect
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ssl_redirect for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_hsts_header_enabled_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) on Load Balancer Listeners (Tier-4 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.hsts_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure hsts_enabled for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_health_checks_strict_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Strict TCP and HTTP Health Checks for Backend Nodes (Tier-4 • Profile O)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.health_check
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure health_check.check_interval for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Load Balancer"]
      requirement["Configure Strict TCP and HTTP Health Checks for Backend Nodes"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0316"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-loadbalancer", label: "Vultr Load Balancer", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_access_logs_archived_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Access Logging to Vultr Object Storage for Request Auditing (Tier-4 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.logging_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure logging_enabled for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_ssl_modern_ciphers_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Modern TLS 1.3 Cyphers on Vultr Load Balancer SSL Termination (Tier-5 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.ssl_redirect
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ssl_redirect for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.
