package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_hsts_header_enabled_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) on Load Balancer Listeners (Tier-5 • Profile R)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.hsts_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure hsts_enabled for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_health_checks_strict_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Strict TCP and HTTP Health Checks for Backend Nodes (Tier-5 • Profile S)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.health_check
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure health_check.check_interval for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Load Balancer"]
      requirement["Configure Strict TCP and HTTP Health Checks for Backend Nodes"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0320"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-loadbalancer", label: "Vultr Load Balancer", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_access_logs_archived_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Access Logging to Vultr Object Storage for Request Auditing (Tier-5 • Profile T)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.logging_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure logging_enabled for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_ssl_modern_ciphers_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Modern TLS 1.3 Cyphers on Vultr Load Balancer SSL Termination (Tier-6 • Profile U)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.ssl_redirect
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ssl_redirect for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_hsts_header_enabled_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) on Load Balancer Listeners (Tier-6 • Profile V)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.hsts_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure hsts_enabled for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_health_checks_strict_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Strict TCP and HTTP Health Checks for Backend Nodes (Tier-6 • Profile W)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.health_check
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure health_check.check_interval for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Load Balancer"]
      requirement["Configure Strict TCP and HTTP Health Checks for Backend Nodes"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0324"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-loadbalancer", label: "Vultr Load Balancer", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_access_logs_archived_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Access Logging to Vultr Object Storage for Request Auditing (Tier-6 • Profile X)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.logging_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure logging_enabled for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_ssl_modern_ciphers_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Modern TLS 1.3 Cyphers on Vultr Load Balancer SSL Termination (Tier-7 • Profile Y)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.ssl_redirect
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ssl_redirect for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_hsts_header_enabled_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) on Load Balancer Listeners (Tier-7 • Profile Z)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.hsts_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure hsts_enabled for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_health_checks_strict_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Strict TCP and HTTP Health Checks for Backend Nodes (Tier-7 • Profile A)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.health_check
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure health_check.check_interval for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Load Balancer"]
      requirement["Configure Strict TCP and HTTP Health Checks for Backend Nodes"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0328"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-loadbalancer", label: "Vultr Load Balancer", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_access_logs_archived_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Access Logging to Vultr Object Storage for Request Auditing (Tier-7 • Profile B)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.logging_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure logging_enabled for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_ssl_modern_ciphers_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Modern TLS 1.3 Cyphers on Vultr Load Balancer SSL Termination (Tier-8 • Profile C)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.ssl_redirect
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ssl_redirect for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_hsts_header_enabled_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) on Load Balancer Listeners (Tier-8 • Profile D)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.hsts_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure hsts_enabled for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_health_checks_strict_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Strict TCP and HTTP Health Checks for Backend Nodes (Tier-8 • Profile E)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.health_check
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure health_check.check_interval for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Load Balancer"]
      requirement["Configure Strict TCP and HTTP Health Checks for Backend Nodes"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0332"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-loadbalancer", label: "Vultr Load Balancer", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_access_logs_archived_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Access Logging to Vultr Object Storage for Request Auditing (Tier-8 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.logging_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure logging_enabled for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_ssl_modern_ciphers_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Modern TLS 1.3 Cyphers on Vultr Load Balancer SSL Termination (Tier-9 • Profile G)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.ssl_redirect
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ssl_redirect for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_hsts_header_enabled_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) on Load Balancer Listeners (Tier-9 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.hsts_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure hsts_enabled for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_health_checks_strict_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Strict TCP and HTTP Health Checks for Backend Nodes (Tier-9 • Profile I)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.health_check
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure health_check.check_interval for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Load Balancer"]
      requirement["Configure Strict TCP and HTTP Health Checks for Backend Nodes"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0336"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-loadbalancer", label: "Vultr Load Balancer", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_access_logs_archived_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Access Logging to Vultr Object Storage for Request Auditing (Tier-9 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.logging_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure logging_enabled for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_ssl_modern_ciphers_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Modern TLS 1.3 Cyphers on Vultr Load Balancer SSL Termination (Tier-10 • Profile K)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.ssl_redirect
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ssl_redirect for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_hsts_header_enabled_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) on Load Balancer Listeners (Tier-10 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.hsts_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure hsts_enabled for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_health_checks_strict_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Strict TCP and HTTP Health Checks for Backend Nodes (Tier-10 • Profile M)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.health_check
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure health_check.check_interval for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Load Balancer"]
      requirement["Configure Strict TCP and HTTP Health Checks for Backend Nodes"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0340"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-loadbalancer", label: "Vultr Load Balancer", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_access_logs_archived_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Access Logging to Vultr Object Storage for Request Auditing (Tier-10 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.logging_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure logging_enabled for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_ssl_modern_ciphers_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Modern TLS 1.3 Cyphers on Vultr Load Balancer SSL Termination (Tier-11 • Profile O)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.ssl_redirect
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ssl_redirect for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_hsts_header_enabled_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) on Load Balancer Listeners (Tier-11 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.hsts_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure hsts_enabled for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_loadbalancer.vultr_loadbalancer_lb_health_checks_strict_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Strict TCP and HTTP Health Checks for Backend Nodes (Tier-11 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.health_check
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure health_check.check_interval for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Load Balancer"]
      requirement["Configure Strict TCP and HTTP Health Checks for Backend Nodes"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0344"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-loadbalancer", label: "Vultr Load Balancer", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_dns.vultr_dns_dns_dnssec_enabled_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce DNSSEC Signature Validation on Vultr Hosted Zones
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_dns_domain"
  not r.change.after.dnssec
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure dnssec for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: DNS discovery and application connection
developer_guide.contract: Zone, record name, record type, answer, TTL and resolver scope
dependencies: An authoritative zone and record set
A resolver and network links for private zones
A separately reachable application endpoint
steps: Create the zone and records with deliberate TTLs.
Configure resolver scope and any private network links.
Test name resolution separately from the application connection.
tests: Query from the actual client environment and inspect the answer and TTL.
Verify a private name is only resolvable from the intended scope.
failures: NXDOMAIN: inspect zone delegation, private links and record name.
Correct answer but failed request: inspect application routing and listener.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_dns.vultr_dns_dns_failover_low_ttl_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Low TTL Values on High-Availability Failover Records
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_dns_record"
  not r.change.after.ttl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ttl for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: DNS discovery and application connection
developer_guide.contract: Zone, record name, record type, answer, TTL and resolver scope
dependencies: An authoritative zone and record set
A resolver and network links for private zones
A separately reachable application endpoint
steps: Create the zone and records with deliberate TTLs.
Configure resolver scope and any private network links.
Test name resolution separately from the application connection.
tests: Query from the actual client environment and inspect the answer and TTL.
Verify a private name is only resolvable from the intended scope.
failures: NXDOMAIN: inspect zone delegation, private links and record name.
Correct answer but failed request: inspect application routing and listener.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_dns.vultr_dns_dns_caa_record_enforced_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce CAA Resource Records to Restrict Permitted Certificate Authorities
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_dns_record"
  not r.change.after.type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure type for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr DNS"]

      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0347"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-dns", label: "Vultr DNS", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: DNS discovery and application connection
developer_guide.contract: Zone, record name, record type, answer, TTL and resolver scope
dependencies: An authoritative zone and record set
A resolver and network links for private zones
A separately reachable application endpoint
steps: Create the zone and records with deliberate TTLs.
Configure resolver scope and any private network links.
Test name resolution separately from the application connection.
tests: Query from the actual client environment and inspect the answer and TTL.
Verify a private name is only resolvable from the intended scope.
failures: NXDOMAIN: inspect zone delegation, private links and record name.
Correct answer but failed request: inspect application routing and listener.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_dns.vultr_dns_dns_dnssec_enabled_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce DNSSEC Signature Validation on Vultr Hosted Zones (Tier-2 • Profile D)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_dns_domain"
  not r.change.after.dnssec
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure dnssec for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]

      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: DNS discovery and application connection
developer_guide.contract: Zone, record name, record type, answer, TTL and resolver scope
dependencies: An authoritative zone and record set
A resolver and network links for private zones
A separately reachable application endpoint
steps: Create the zone and records with deliberate TTLs.
Configure resolver scope and any private network links.
Test name resolution separately from the application connection.
tests: Query from the actual client environment and inspect the answer and TTL.
Verify a private name is only resolvable from the intended scope.
failures: NXDOMAIN: inspect zone delegation, private links and record name.
Correct answer but failed request: inspect application routing and listener.

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_dns.vultr_dns_dns_failover_low_ttl_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Low TTL Values on High-Availability Failover Records (Tier-2 • Profile E)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_dns_record"
  not r.change.after.ttl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ttl for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: DNS discovery and application connection
developer_guide.contract: Zone, record name, record type, answer, TTL and resolver scope
dependencies: An authoritative zone and record set
A resolver and network links for private zones
A separately reachable application endpoint
steps: Create the zone and records with deliberate TTLs.
Configure resolver scope and any private network links.
Test name resolution separately from the application connection.
tests: Query from the actual client environment and inspect the answer and TTL.
Verify a private name is only resolvable from the intended scope.
failures: NXDOMAIN: inspect zone delegation, private links and record name.
Correct answer but failed request: inspect application routing and listener.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_dns.vultr_dns_dns_caa_record_enforced_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce CAA Resource Records to Restrict Permitted Certificate Authorities (Tier-2 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_dns_record"
  not r.change.after.type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure type for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: DNS discovery and application connection
developer_guide.contract: Zone, record name, record type, answer, TTL and resolver scope
dependencies: An authoritative zone and record set
A resolver and network links for private zones
A separately reachable application endpoint
steps: Create the zone and records with deliberate TTLs.
Configure resolver scope and any private network links.
Test name resolution separately from the application connection.
tests: Query from the actual client environment and inspect the answer and TTL.
Verify a private name is only resolvable from the intended scope.
failures: NXDOMAIN: inspect zone delegation, private links and record name.
Correct answer but failed request: inspect application routing and listener.

package vultr.vultr_dns.vultr_dns_dns_dnssec_enabled_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce DNSSEC Signature Validation on Vultr Hosted Zones (Tier-3 • Profile G)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_dns_domain"
  not r.change.after.dnssec
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure dnssec for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr DNS"]
      requirement["Enforce DNSSEC Signature Validation on Vultr Hosted Zones"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0351"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-dns", label: "Vultr DNS", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: DNS discovery and application connection
developer_guide.contract: Zone, record name, record type, answer, TTL and resolver scope
dependencies: An authoritative zone and record set
A resolver and network links for private zones
A separately reachable application endpoint
steps: Create the zone and records with deliberate TTLs.
Configure resolver scope and any private network links.
Test name resolution separately from the application connection.
tests: Query from the actual client environment and inspect the answer and TTL.
Verify a private name is only resolvable from the intended scope.
failures: NXDOMAIN: inspect zone delegation, private links and record name.
Correct answer but failed request: inspect application routing and listener.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_dns.vultr_dns_dns_failover_low_ttl_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Low TTL Values on High-Availability Failover Records (Tier-3 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_dns_record"
  not r.change.after.ttl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ttl for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: DNS discovery and application connection
developer_guide.contract: Zone, record name, record type, answer, TTL and resolver scope
dependencies: An authoritative zone and record set
A resolver and network links for private zones
A separately reachable application endpoint
steps: Create the zone and records with deliberate TTLs.
Configure resolver scope and any private network links.
Test name resolution separately from the application connection.
tests: Query from the actual client environment and inspect the answer and TTL.
Verify a private name is only resolvable from the intended scope.
failures: NXDOMAIN: inspect zone delegation, private links and record name.
Correct answer but failed request: inspect application routing and listener.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_dns.vultr_dns_dns_caa_record_enforced_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce CAA Resource Records to Restrict Permitted Certificate Authorities (Tier-3 • Profile I)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_dns_record"
  not r.change.after.type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure type for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end

      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]

      requirement --> check

      check -->|Yes| review
    end

      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-dns", label: "Vultr DNS", h: 64, pos: "b" }

      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }

      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end
