deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_logging"
  not r.change.after.export_target
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure export_target for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])

package vultr.vultr_logging.vultr_logging_logging_unauthorized_api_alert_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Audit Log Alerting on Unauthorized Management API Calls (Tier-12 • Profile I)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_logging"
  not r.change.after.alert_on_403
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure alert_on_403 for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.

package vultr.vultr_logging.vultr_logging_logging_immutable_retention_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Retain Immutable Audit Logs for 365 Days for Regulatory Compliance (Tier-12 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_logging"
  not r.change.after.retention_days
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure retention_days for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: API event collection
developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.

vultr-cli account info

vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_logging"
  not r.change.after.export_target
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure export_target for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention

A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.

Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.

package vultr.vultr_logging.vultr_logging_logging_unauthorized_api_alert_t13

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Audit Log Alerting on Unauthorized Management API Calls (Tier-13 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_logging"
  not r.change.after.alert_on_403
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure alert_on_403 for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

package vultr.vultr_logging.vultr_logging_logging_immutable_retention_t13

default allow = false

# Rule: Retain Immutable Audit Logs for 365 Days for Regulatory Compliance (Tier-13 • Profile M)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_logging"
  not r.change.after.retention_days
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure retention_days for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: API event collection
developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.

package vultr.vultr_logging.vultr_logging_logging_stream_to_s3_t14

default allow = false

# Rule: Stream Vultr Activity Logs to Long-Term Encrypted Object Storage (Tier-14 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_logging"
  not r.change.after.export_target
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure export_target for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.

package vultr.vultr_logging.vultr_logging_logging_unauthorized_api_alert_t14

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Audit Log Alerting on Unauthorized Management API Calls (Tier-14 • Profile O)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_logging"
  not r.change.after.alert_on_403
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure alert_on_403 for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: API event collection
developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_logging.vultr_logging_logging_immutable_retention_t14

default allow = false

# Rule: Retain Immutable Audit Logs for 365 Days for Regulatory Compliance (Tier-14 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_logging"
  not r.change.after.retention_days
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure retention_days for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Activity Logs"]
      requirement["Retain Immutable Audit Logs for 365 Days for Regulatory Compliance"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0472"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr Activity Logs", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

package vultr.vultr_monitoring.vultr_monitoring_monitoring_resource_thresholds_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure CPU and Memory Exhaustion Alerts on Compute Instances
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.cpu_threshold_percent
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure cpu_threshold_percent for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_monitoring.vultr_monitoring_monitoring_secops_webhook_route_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Route High-Severity Monitoring Alerts to SecOps PagerDuty Webhook
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.webhook_url
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure webhook_url for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_monitoring.vultr_monitoring_monitoring_firewall_drop_metrics_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Monitor Ingress Drop Rates on Cloud Firewall Groups for DDoS Patterns
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.track_firewall_drops
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure track_firewall_drops for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

package vultr.vultr_monitoring.vultr_monitoring_monitoring_resource_thresholds_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure CPU and Memory Exhaustion Alerts on Compute Instances (Tier-2 • Profile D)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.cpu_threshold_percent
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure cpu_threshold_percent for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_monitoring.vultr_monitoring_monitoring_secops_webhook_route_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Route High-Severity Monitoring Alerts to SecOps PagerDuty Webhook (Tier-2 • Profile E)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.webhook_url
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure webhook_url for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_monitoring.vultr_monitoring_monitoring_firewall_drop_metrics_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Monitor Ingress Drop Rates on Cloud Firewall Groups for DDoS Patterns (Tier-2 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.track_firewall_drops
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure track_firewall_drops for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

# Rule: Configure CPU and Memory Exhaustion Alerts on Compute Instances (Tier-3 • Profile G)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.cpu_threshold_percent
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure cpu_threshold_percent for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_monitoring.vultr_monitoring_monitoring_secops_webhook_route_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Route High-Severity Monitoring Alerts to SecOps PagerDuty Webhook (Tier-3 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.webhook_url
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure webhook_url for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Monitoring"]
      requirement["Route High-Severity Monitoring Alerts to SecOps PagerDuty Webhook"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0481"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-monitoring", label: "Vultr Monitoring", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.track_firewall_drops

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure CPU and Memory Exhaustion Alerts on Compute Instances (Tier-4 • Profile J)

  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.cpu_threshold_percent

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_monitoring.vultr_monitoring_monitoring_secops_webhook_route_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Route High-Severity Monitoring Alerts to SecOps PagerDuty Webhook (Tier-4 • Profile K)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.webhook_url
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure webhook_url for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_monitoring.vultr_monitoring_monitoring_firewall_drop_metrics_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Monitor Ingress Drop Rates on Cloud Firewall Groups for DDoS Patterns (Tier-4 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.track_firewall_drops
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure track_firewall_drops for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Monitoring"]
      requirement["Monitor Ingress Drop Rates on Cloud Firewall Groups for DDoS Patterns"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0485"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-monitoring", label: "Vultr Monitoring", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_monitoring.vultr_monitoring_monitoring_secops_webhook_route_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Route High-Severity Monitoring Alerts to SecOps PagerDuty Webhook (Tier-5 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.webhook_url
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure webhook_url for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_monitoring.vultr_monitoring_monitoring_firewall_drop_metrics_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Monitor Ingress Drop Rates on Cloud Firewall Groups for DDoS Patterns (Tier-5 • Profile O)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.track_firewall_drops
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure track_firewall_drops for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_monitoring.vultr_monitoring_monitoring_resource_thresholds_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure CPU and Memory Exhaustion Alerts on Compute Instances (Tier-6 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.cpu_threshold_percent
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure cpu_threshold_percent for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Monitoring"]
      requirement["Configure CPU and Memory Exhaustion Alerts on Compute Instances"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0489"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-monitoring", label: "Vultr Monitoring", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.

package vultr.vultr_monitoring.vultr_monitoring_monitoring_secops_webhook_route_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Route High-Severity Monitoring Alerts to SecOps PagerDuty Webhook (Tier-6 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.webhook_url
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure webhook_url for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.track_firewall_drops
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure track_firewall_drops for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_monitoring.vultr_monitoring_monitoring_secops_webhook_route_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Route High-Severity Monitoring Alerts to SecOps PagerDuty Webhook (Tier-7 • Profile T)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.webhook_url
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure webhook_url for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

package vultr.vultr_monitoring.vultr_monitoring_monitoring_firewall_drop_metrics_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Monitor Ingress Drop Rates on Cloud Firewall Groups for DDoS Patterns (Tier-7 • Profile U)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.track_firewall_drops
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure track_firewall_drops for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_monitoring.vultr_monitoring_monitoring_secops_webhook_route_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Route High-Severity Monitoring Alerts to SecOps PagerDuty Webhook (Tier-8 • Profile W)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.webhook_url
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure webhook_url for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.track_firewall_drops
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure track_firewall_drops for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_monitoring.vultr_monitoring_monitoring_resource_thresholds_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure CPU and Memory Exhaustion Alerts on Compute Instances (Tier-9 • Profile Y)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.cpu_threshold_percent
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure cpu_threshold_percent for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

flowchart TB

      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Monitoring"]

      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0498"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-monitoring", label: "Vultr Monitoring", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }

      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_monitoring.vultr_monitoring_monitoring_secops_webhook_route_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Route High-Severity Monitoring Alerts to SecOps PagerDuty Webhook (Tier-9 • Profile Z)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.webhook_url
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure webhook_url for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_monitoring.vultr_monitoring_monitoring_firewall_drop_metrics_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Monitor Ingress Drop Rates on Cloud Firewall Groups for DDoS Patterns (Tier-9 • Profile A)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.track_firewall_drops
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure track_firewall_drops for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

# Rule: Configure CPU and Memory Exhaustion Alerts on Compute Instances (Tier-10 • Profile B)

deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.cpu_threshold_percent
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure cpu_threshold_percent for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_monitoring.vultr_monitoring_monitoring_secops_webhook_route_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Route High-Severity Monitoring Alerts to SecOps PagerDuty Webhook (Tier-10 • Profile C)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.webhook_url
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure webhook_url for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Monitoring"]
      requirement["Route High-Severity Monitoring Alerts to SecOps PagerDuty Webhook"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0502"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-monitoring", label: "Vultr Monitoring", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure CPU and Memory Exhaustion Alerts on Compute Instances (Tier-11 • Profile E)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.cpu_threshold_percent
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure cpu_threshold_percent for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_monitoring.vultr_monitoring_monitoring_secops_webhook_route_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Route High-Severity Monitoring Alerts to SecOps PagerDuty Webhook (Tier-11 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.webhook_url
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure webhook_url for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
