developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_monitoring.vultr_monitoring_monitoring_firewall_drop_metrics_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Monitor Ingress Drop Rates on Cloud Firewall Groups for DDoS Patterns (Tier-11 • Profile G)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.track_firewall_drops
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure track_firewall_drops for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"

package vultr.vultr_monitoring.vultr_monitoring_monitoring_resource_thresholds_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure CPU and Memory Exhaustion Alerts on Compute Instances (Tier-12 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.cpu_threshold_percent
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure cpu_threshold_percent for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_monitoring.vultr_monitoring_monitoring_secops_webhook_route_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Route High-Severity Monitoring Alerts to SecOps PagerDuty Webhook (Tier-12 • Profile I)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.webhook_url
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure webhook_url for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_monitoring.vultr_monitoring_monitoring_firewall_drop_metrics_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Monitor Ingress Drop Rates on Cloud Firewall Groups for DDoS Patterns (Tier-12 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.track_firewall_drops
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure track_firewall_drops for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.cpu_threshold_percent
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure cpu_threshold_percent for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_monitoring.vultr_monitoring_monitoring_secops_webhook_route_t13

default allow = false

# Rule: Route High-Severity Monitoring Alerts to SecOps PagerDuty Webhook (Tier-13 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.webhook_url
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure webhook_url for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Monitoring"]
      requirement["Route High-Severity Monitoring Alerts to SecOps PagerDuty Webhook"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0511"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-monitoring", label: "Vultr Monitoring", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

default allow = false

# Rule: Monitor Ingress Drop Rates on Cloud Firewall Groups for DDoS Patterns (Tier-13 • Profile M)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.track_firewall_drops
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure track_firewall_drops for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure CPU and Memory Exhaustion Alerts on Compute Instances (Tier-14 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.cpu_threshold_percent
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure cpu_threshold_percent for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_monitoring.vultr_monitoring_monitoring_secops_webhook_route_t14

default allow = false

# Rule: Route High-Severity Monitoring Alerts to SecOps PagerDuty Webhook (Tier-14 • Profile O)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.webhook_url
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure webhook_url for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_monitoring.vultr_monitoring_monitoring_firewall_drop_metrics_t14

default allow = false

# Rule: Monitor Ingress Drop Rates on Cloud Firewall Groups for DDoS Patterns (Tier-14 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_monitoring"
  not r.change.after.track_firewall_drops
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure track_firewall_drops for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Monitoring"]
      requirement["Monitor Ingress Drop Rates on Cloud Firewall Groups for DDoS Patterns"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0515"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-monitoring", label: "Vultr Monitoring", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_security.vultr_security_security_ddos_shield_always_on_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Activate Always-On 100 Gbps DDoS Mitigation on Public IP Addresses
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.ddos_protection
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ddos_protection for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.

vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_security.vultr_security_security_geo_ip_filtering_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Block Malicious Geo-IP Ranges at Edge Perimeter Firewalls
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_group"
  not r.change.after.geo_blocking
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure geo_blocking for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.

vultr-cli account info

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_security.vultr_security_security_threat_intel_feed_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Threat Intelligence Feed Integration for Real-Time Blacklisting
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_group"
  not r.change.after.threat_intelligence_sync
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure threat_intelligence_sync for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr DDoS Protection"]
      requirement["Enforce Threat Intelligence Feed Integration for Real-Time Blacklisting"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0519"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-security", label: "Vultr DDoS Protection", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_security.vultr_security_security_ddos_shield_always_on_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Activate Always-On 100 Gbps DDoS Mitigation on Public IP Addresses (Tier-2 • Profile D)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.ddos_protection
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ddos_protection for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.

vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_security.vultr_security_security_geo_ip_filtering_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Block Malicious Geo-IP Ranges at Edge Perimeter Firewalls (Tier-2 • Profile E)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_group"
  not r.change.after.geo_blocking
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure geo_blocking for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_security.vultr_security_security_threat_intel_feed_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Threat Intelligence Feed Integration for Real-Time Blacklisting (Tier-2 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_group"
  not r.change.after.threat_intelligence_sync
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure threat_intelligence_sync for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

    end

      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_security.vultr_security_security_ddos_shield_always_on_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Activate Always-On 100 Gbps DDoS Mitigation on Public IP Addresses (Tier-3 • Profile G)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.ddos_protection
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ddos_protection for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_security.vultr_security_security_geo_ip_filtering_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Block Malicious Geo-IP Ranges at Edge Perimeter Firewalls (Tier-3 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_group"
  not r.change.after.geo_blocking
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure geo_blocking for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_security.vultr_security_security_threat_intel_feed_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Threat Intelligence Feed Integration for Real-Time Blacklisting (Tier-3 • Profile I)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_group"
  not r.change.after.threat_intelligence_sync
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure threat_intelligence_sync for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.

vultr-cli account info

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_security.vultr_security_security_ddos_shield_always_on_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Activate Always-On 100 Gbps DDoS Mitigation on Public IP Addresses (Tier-4 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.ddos_protection
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ddos_protection for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr DDoS Protection"]
      requirement["Activate Always-On 100 Gbps DDoS Mitigation on Public IP Addresses"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0526"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-security", label: "Vultr DDoS Protection", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_security.vultr_security_security_geo_ip_filtering_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Block Malicious Geo-IP Ranges at Edge Perimeter Firewalls (Tier-4 • Profile K)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_group"
  not r.change.after.geo_blocking
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure geo_blocking for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_security.vultr_security_security_threat_intel_feed_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Threat Intelligence Feed Integration for Real-Time Blacklisting (Tier-4 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_group"
  not r.change.after.threat_intelligence_sync
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure threat_intelligence_sync for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_security.vultr_security_security_ddos_shield_always_on_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Activate Always-On 100 Gbps DDoS Mitigation on Public IP Addresses (Tier-5 • Profile M)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.ddos_protection
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ddos_protection for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.

vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.

package vultr.vultr_security.vultr_security_security_geo_ip_filtering_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Block Malicious Geo-IP Ranges at Edge Perimeter Firewalls (Tier-5 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_group"
  not r.change.after.geo_blocking
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure geo_blocking for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.

checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_security.vultr_security_security_threat_intel_feed_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Threat Intelligence Feed Integration for Real-Time Blacklisting (Tier-5 • Profile O)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_group"
  not r.change.after.threat_intelligence_sync
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure threat_intelligence_sync for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.

: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"

developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_security.vultr_security_security_ddos_shield_always_on_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Activate Always-On 100 Gbps DDoS Mitigation on Public IP Addresses (Tier-6 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.ddos_protection
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ddos_protection for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end

      requirement --> check

    end

      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-security", label: "Vultr DDoS Protection", h: 64, pos: "b" }

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.

vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_security.vultr_security_security_geo_ip_filtering_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Block Malicious Geo-IP Ranges at Edge Perimeter Firewalls (Tier-6 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_group"
  not r.change.after.geo_blocking
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure geo_blocking for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr DDoS Protection"]
      requirement["Block Malicious Geo-IP Ranges at Edge Perimeter Firewalls"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0533"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-security", label: "Vultr DDoS Protection", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_security.vultr_security_security_threat_intel_feed_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Threat Intelligence Feed Integration for Real-Time Blacklisting (Tier-6 • Profile R)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_group"
  not r.change.after.threat_intelligence_sync
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure threat_intelligence_sync for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_security.vultr_security_security_ddos_shield_always_on_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Activate Always-On 100 Gbps DDoS Mitigation on Public IP Addresses (Tier-7 • Profile S)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.ddos_protection
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ddos_protection for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_security.vultr_security_security_geo_ip_filtering_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Block Malicious Geo-IP Ranges at Edge Perimeter Firewalls (Tier-7 • Profile T)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_group"
  not r.change.after.geo_blocking
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure geo_blocking for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_security.vultr_security_security_threat_intel_feed_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Threat Intelligence Feed Integration for Real-Time Blacklisting (Tier-7 • Profile U)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_group"
  not r.change.after.threat_intelligence_sync
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure threat_intelligence_sync for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_security.vultr_security_security_ddos_shield_always_on_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Activate Always-On 100 Gbps DDoS Mitigation on Public IP Addresses (Tier-8 • Profile V)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.ddos_protection
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ddos_protection for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_security.vultr_security_security_geo_ip_filtering_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Block Malicious Geo-IP Ranges at Edge Perimeter Firewalls (Tier-8 • Profile W)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_group"
  not r.change.after.geo_blocking
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure geo_blocking for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0539"]
      requirement --> check

      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-security", label: "Vultr DDoS Protection", h: 64, pos: "b" }

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.

vultr-cli account info

vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_security.vultr_security_security_threat_intel_feed_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Threat Intelligence Feed Integration for Real-Time Blacklisting (Tier-8 • Profile X)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_firewall_group"
  not r.change.after.threat_intelligence_sync
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure threat_intelligence_sync for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr DDoS Protection"]
      requirement["Enforce Threat Intelligence Feed Integration for Real-Time Blacklisting"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0540"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-security", label: "Vultr DDoS Protection", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end
