package vultr.vultr_block_storage.vultr_block_storage_block_storage_nightly_snapshots_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Automated Nightly Volume Snapshots with Cross-DC Duplication (Tier-2 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.auto_snapshot
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure auto_snapshot for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Block Storage"]
      requirement["Configure Automated Nightly Volume Snapshots with Cross-DC Duplication"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0608"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-block-storage", label: "Vultr Block Storage", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

package vultr.vultr_block_storage.vultr_block_storage_block_storage_encrypted_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce LUKS / Hardware-Level Encryption on NVMe Block Storage Volumes (Tier-3 • Profile G)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.encrypted
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure encrypted for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_block_storage.vultr_block_storage_block_storage_vpc_instance_bind_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Attach NVMe Storage Exclusively to Instances Within the Same VPC Network (Tier-3 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.attached_to_instance
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure attached_to_instance for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_block_storage.vultr_block_storage_block_storage_nightly_snapshots_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Automated Nightly Volume Snapshots with Cross-DC Duplication (Tier-3 • Profile I)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.auto_snapshot
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure auto_snapshot for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

package vultr.vultr_block_storage.vultr_block_storage_block_storage_encrypted_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce LUKS / Hardware-Level Encryption on NVMe Block Storage Volumes (Tier-4 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.encrypted
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure encrypted for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_block_storage.vultr_block_storage_block_storage_vpc_instance_bind_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Attach NVMe Storage Exclusively to Instances Within the Same VPC Network (Tier-4 • Profile K)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.attached_to_instance
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure attached_to_instance for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_block_storage.vultr_block_storage_block_storage_nightly_snapshots_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Automated Nightly Volume Snapshots with Cross-DC Duplication (Tier-4 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.auto_snapshot
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure auto_snapshot for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Block Storage"]
      requirement["Configure Automated Nightly Volume Snapshots with Cross-DC Duplication"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0614"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-block-storage", label: "Vultr Block Storage", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

package vultr.vultr_block_storage.vultr_block_storage_block_storage_encrypted_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce LUKS / Hardware-Level Encryption on NVMe Block Storage Volumes (Tier-5 • Profile M)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.encrypted
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure encrypted for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_block_storage.vultr_block_storage_block_storage_vpc_instance_bind_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Attach NVMe Storage Exclusively to Instances Within the Same VPC Network (Tier-5 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.attached_to_instance
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure attached_to_instance for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_block_storage.vultr_block_storage_block_storage_nightly_snapshots_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Automated Nightly Volume Snapshots with Cross-DC Duplication (Tier-5 • Profile O)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.auto_snapshot
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure auto_snapshot for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Block Storage"]
      requirement["Configure Automated Nightly Volume Snapshots with Cross-DC Duplication"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0617"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-block-storage", label: "Vultr Block Storage", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

package vultr.vultr_block_storage.vultr_block_storage_block_storage_encrypted_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce LUKS / Hardware-Level Encryption on NVMe Block Storage Volumes (Tier-6 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.encrypted
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure encrypted for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_block_storage.vultr_block_storage_block_storage_vpc_instance_bind_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Attach NVMe Storage Exclusively to Instances Within the Same VPC Network (Tier-6 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.attached_to_instance
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure attached_to_instance for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_block_storage.vultr_block_storage_block_storage_nightly_snapshots_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Automated Nightly Volume Snapshots with Cross-DC Duplication (Tier-6 • Profile R)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.auto_snapshot
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure auto_snapshot for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

package vultr.vultr_block_storage.vultr_block_storage_block_storage_encrypted_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce LUKS / Hardware-Level Encryption on NVMe Block Storage Volumes (Tier-7 • Profile S)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.encrypted
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure encrypted for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_block_storage.vultr_block_storage_block_storage_vpc_instance_bind_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Attach NVMe Storage Exclusively to Instances Within the Same VPC Network (Tier-7 • Profile T)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.attached_to_instance
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure attached_to_instance for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

package vultr.vultr_block_storage.vultr_block_storage_block_storage_nightly_snapshots_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Automated Nightly Volume Snapshots with Cross-DC Duplication (Tier-7 • Profile U)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.auto_snapshot
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure auto_snapshot for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

package vultr.vultr_block_storage.vultr_block_storage_block_storage_encrypted_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce LUKS / Hardware-Level Encryption on NVMe Block Storage Volumes (Tier-8 • Profile V)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.encrypted
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure encrypted for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_block_storage.vultr_block_storage_block_storage_vpc_instance_bind_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Attach NVMe Storage Exclusively to Instances Within the Same VPC Network (Tier-8 • Profile W)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.attached_to_instance
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure attached_to_instance for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_block_storage.vultr_block_storage_block_storage_nightly_snapshots_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Automated Nightly Volume Snapshots with Cross-DC Duplication (Tier-8 • Profile X)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.auto_snapshot
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure auto_snapshot for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

package vultr.vultr_block_storage.vultr_block_storage_block_storage_encrypted_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce LUKS / Hardware-Level Encryption on NVMe Block Storage Volumes (Tier-9 • Profile Y)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.encrypted
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure encrypted for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_block_storage.vultr_block_storage_block_storage_vpc_instance_bind_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Attach NVMe Storage Exclusively to Instances Within the Same VPC Network (Tier-9 • Profile Z)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.attached_to_instance
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure attached_to_instance for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Automated Nightly Volume Snapshots with Cross-DC Duplication (Tier-9 • Profile A)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.auto_snapshot
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure auto_snapshot for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

package vultr.vultr_block_storage.vultr_block_storage_block_storage_encrypted_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce LUKS / Hardware-Level Encryption on NVMe Block Storage Volumes (Tier-10 • Profile B)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.encrypted
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure encrypted for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_block_storage.vultr_block_storage_block_storage_vpc_instance_bind_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Attach NVMe Storage Exclusively to Instances Within the Same VPC Network (Tier-10 • Profile C)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.attached_to_instance
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure attached_to_instance for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.

package vultr.vultr_block_storage.vultr_block_storage_block_storage_nightly_snapshots_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Automated Nightly Volume Snapshots with Cross-DC Duplication (Tier-10 • Profile D)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.auto_snapshot
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure auto_snapshot for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

package vultr.vultr_block_storage.vultr_block_storage_block_storage_encrypted_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce LUKS / Hardware-Level Encryption on NVMe Block Storage Volumes (Tier-11 • Profile E)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.encrypted
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure encrypted for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_block_storage.vultr_block_storage_block_storage_vpc_instance_bind_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Attach NVMe Storage Exclusively to Instances Within the Same VPC Network (Tier-11 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.attached_to_instance
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure attached_to_instance for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

package vultr.vultr_block_storage.vultr_block_storage_block_storage_encrypted_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce LUKS / Hardware-Level Encryption on NVMe Block Storage Volumes (Tier-12 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.encrypted
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure encrypted for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_block_storage.vultr_block_storage_block_storage_vpc_instance_bind_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Attach NVMe Storage Exclusively to Instances Within the Same VPC Network (Tier-12 • Profile I)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.attached_to_instance
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure attached_to_instance for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.

package vultr.vultr_block_storage.vultr_block_storage_block_storage_nightly_snapshots_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Automated Nightly Volume Snapshots with Cross-DC Duplication (Tier-12 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.auto_snapshot
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure auto_snapshot for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

package vultr.vultr_block_storage.vultr_block_storage_block_storage_encrypted_t13

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce LUKS / Hardware-Level Encryption on NVMe Block Storage Volumes (Tier-13 • Profile K)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.encrypted
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure encrypted for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_block_storage.vultr_block_storage_block_storage_vpc_instance_bind_t13

default allow = false

# Rule: Attach NVMe Storage Exclusively to Instances Within the Same VPC Network (Tier-13 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.attached_to_instance
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure attached_to_instance for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Automated Nightly Volume Snapshots with Cross-DC Duplication (Tier-13 • Profile M)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.auto_snapshot
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure auto_snapshot for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

package vultr.vultr_block_storage.vultr_block_storage_block_storage_encrypted_t14

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce LUKS / Hardware-Level Encryption on NVMe Block Storage Volumes (Tier-14 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.encrypted
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure encrypted for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_block_storage.vultr_block_storage_block_storage_vpc_instance_bind_t14

default allow = false

# Rule: Attach NVMe Storage Exclusively to Instances Within the Same VPC Network (Tier-14 • Profile O)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.attached_to_instance
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure attached_to_instance for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.

package vultr.vultr_block_storage.vultr_block_storage_block_storage_nightly_snapshots_t14

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Automated Nightly Volume Snapshots with Cross-DC Duplication (Tier-14 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.auto_snapshot
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure auto_snapshot for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

package vultr.vultr_block_storage.vultr_block_storage_block_storage_encrypted_t15

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce LUKS / Hardware-Level Encryption on NVMe Block Storage Volumes (Tier-15 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_block_storage"
  not r.change.after.encrypted
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure encrypted for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_container_registry.vultr_container_registry_registry_scan_on_push_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Vulnerability Scanning on All Pushed Container Images in VCR
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_container_registry"
  not r.change.after.scan_on_push
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure scan_on_push for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Container build, provenance and runtime consumption
developer_guide.contract: Image digest, signer identity, SBOM format and admission policy
dependencies: A build runner, registry and runtime pull identity
Chosen scan, signing and verification tools
steps: Build and scan the image; record its immutable digest.
Publish required signatures or attestations under an explicit trust policy.
Verify the digest and policy at the point of consumption.
tests: Verify a trusted digest and reject an unexpected signer or tampered artifact.
Run the image with the intended filesystem, user and secret restrictions.
failures: Verification failure: inspect digest, issuer, signer identity and trust roots.
Runtime failure: inspect image architecture, entrypoint and required writable paths.

vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify artifact digest, trusted signer identity, and relevant attestations
An image signature establishes provenance only under the configured trust policy. Scan results, deployment admission, and runtime restrictions remain separate controls.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_container_registry.vultr_container_registry_registry_private_repositories_only_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Disable Public Repository Access and Require Token Authentication
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_container_registry"
  not r.change.after.public_access
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure public_access for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Container Registry"]
      requirement["Disable Public Repository Access and Require Token Authentication"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0647"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-container-registry", label: "Vultr Container Registry", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end
