opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_disable_dangerous_commands_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Disable Dangerous Redis Commands via Configuration Parameters (Tier-3 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.disabled_commands
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure disabled_commands for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application query and data access
developer_guide.contract: Collection or table, partition key, query shape and consistency model
dependencies: A provisioned data store and scoped application identity
A query or item access pattern and an explicit retry budget
steps: Create tables, containers or datasets with the intended partitioning.
Grant only the required query or item operations.
Handle throttling, pagination and idempotent writes in the application.
tests: Test representative queries and partition distribution.
Exercise throttling, duplicate delivery and access to a disallowed dataset.
failures: Throttling: inspect partition hotspots, request units or quota.
Missing rows: inspect key selection, consistency and query permissions.

vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_vpc_only_binding_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Bind Managed Redis Exclusively to VPC 2.0 Internal IP Interfaces (Tier-3 • Profile I)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.vpc2_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc2_id for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Redis"]
      requirement["Bind Managed Redis Exclusively to VPC 2.0 Internal IP Interfaces"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0740"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-redis", label: "Vultr Managed Redis", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application query and data access
developer_guide.contract: Collection or table, partition key, query shape and consistency model
dependencies: A provisioned data store and scoped application identity
A query or item access pattern and an explicit retry budget
steps: Create tables, containers or datasets with the intended partitioning.
Grant only the required query or item operations.
Handle throttling, pagination and idempotent writes in the application.
tests: Test representative queries and partition distribution.
Exercise throttling, duplicate delivery and access to a disallowed dataset.
failures: Throttling: inspect partition hotspots, request units or quota.
Missing rows: inspect key selection, consistency and query permissions.

package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_auth_and_tls_enforced_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce TLS Encryption and Require Auth Password on Managed Redis (Tier-4 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.require_ssl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure require_ssl for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application query and data access
developer_guide.contract: Collection or table, partition key, query shape and consistency model
dependencies: A provisioned data store and scoped application identity
A query or item access pattern and an explicit retry budget
steps: Create tables, containers or datasets with the intended partitioning.
Grant only the required query or item operations.
Handle throttling, pagination and idempotent writes in the application.
tests: Test representative queries and partition distribution.
Exercise throttling, duplicate delivery and access to a disallowed dataset.
failures: Throttling: inspect partition hotspots, request units or quota.
Missing rows: inspect key selection, consistency and query permissions.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_disable_dangerous_commands_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Disable Dangerous Redis Commands via Configuration Parameters (Tier-4 • Profile K)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.disabled_commands
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure disabled_commands for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

A query or item access pattern and an explicit retry budget
steps: Create tables, containers or datasets with the intended partitioning.
Grant only the required query or item operations.
Handle throttling, pagination and idempotent writes in the application.
tests: Test representative queries and partition distribution.
Exercise throttling, duplicate delivery and access to a disallowed dataset.
failures: Throttling: inspect partition hotspots, request units or quota.
Missing rows: inspect key selection, consistency and query permissions.

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_vpc_only_binding_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Bind Managed Redis Exclusively to VPC 2.0 Internal IP Interfaces (Tier-4 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.vpc2_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc2_id for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application query and data access
developer_guide.contract: Collection or table, partition key, query shape and consistency model
dependencies: A provisioned data store and scoped application identity
A query or item access pattern and an explicit retry budget
steps: Create tables, containers or datasets with the intended partitioning.
Grant only the required query or item operations.
Handle throttling, pagination and idempotent writes in the application.
tests: Test representative queries and partition distribution.
Exercise throttling, duplicate delivery and access to a disallowed dataset.
failures: Throttling: inspect partition hotspots, request units or quota.
Missing rows: inspect key selection, consistency and query permissions.

checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_auth_and_tls_enforced_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce TLS Encryption and Require Auth Password on Managed Redis (Tier-5 • Profile M)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.require_ssl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure require_ssl for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application query and data access
developer_guide.contract: Collection or table, partition key, query shape and consistency model
dependencies: A provisioned data store and scoped application identity
A query or item access pattern and an explicit retry budget
steps: Create tables, containers or datasets with the intended partitioning.
Grant only the required query or item operations.
Handle throttling, pagination and idempotent writes in the application.
tests: Test representative queries and partition distribution.
Exercise throttling, duplicate delivery and access to a disallowed dataset.
failures: Throttling: inspect partition hotspots, request units or quota.
Missing rows: inspect key selection, consistency and query permissions.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_disable_dangerous_commands_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Disable Dangerous Redis Commands via Configuration Parameters (Tier-5 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.disabled_commands
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure disabled_commands for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Redis"]
      requirement["Disable Dangerous Redis Commands via Configuration Parameters"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0745"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-redis", label: "Vultr Managed Redis", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_vpc_only_binding_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Bind Managed Redis Exclusively to VPC 2.0 Internal IP Interfaces (Tier-5 • Profile O)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.vpc2_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc2_id for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application query and data access
developer_guide.contract: Collection or table, partition key, query shape and consistency model
dependencies: A provisioned data store and scoped application identity
A query or item access pattern and an explicit retry budget
steps: Create tables, containers or datasets with the intended partitioning.
Grant only the required query or item operations.
Handle throttling, pagination and idempotent writes in the application.
tests: Test representative queries and partition distribution.
Exercise throttling, duplicate delivery and access to a disallowed dataset.
failures: Throttling: inspect partition hotspots, request units or quota.
Missing rows: inspect key selection, consistency and query permissions.

vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_auth_and_tls_enforced_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce TLS Encryption and Require Auth Password on Managed Redis (Tier-6 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.require_ssl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure require_ssl for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application query and data access
developer_guide.contract: Collection or table, partition key, query shape and consistency model
dependencies: A provisioned data store and scoped application identity
A query or item access pattern and an explicit retry budget
steps: Create tables, containers or datasets with the intended partitioning.
Grant only the required query or item operations.
Handle throttling, pagination and idempotent writes in the application.
tests: Test representative queries and partition distribution.
Exercise throttling, duplicate delivery and access to a disallowed dataset.
failures: Throttling: inspect partition hotspots, request units or quota.
Missing rows: inspect key selection, consistency and query permissions.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_disable_dangerous_commands_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Disable Dangerous Redis Commands via Configuration Parameters (Tier-6 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.disabled_commands
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure disabled_commands for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Redis"]
      requirement["Disable Dangerous Redis Commands via Configuration Parameters"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0748"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-redis", label: "Vultr Managed Redis", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.contract: Collection or table, partition key, query shape and consistency model
dependencies: A provisioned data store and scoped application identity
A query or item access pattern and an explicit retry budget
steps: Create tables, containers or datasets with the intended partitioning.
Grant only the required query or item operations.
Handle throttling, pagination and idempotent writes in the application.
tests: Test representative queries and partition distribution.
Exercise throttling, duplicate delivery and access to a disallowed dataset.
failures: Throttling: inspect partition hotspots, request units or quota.
Missing rows: inspect key selection, consistency and query permissions.

package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_vpc_only_binding_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Bind Managed Redis Exclusively to VPC 2.0 Internal IP Interfaces (Tier-6 • Profile R)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.vpc2_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc2_id for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application query and data access
developer_guide.contract: Collection or table, partition key, query shape and consistency model
dependencies: A provisioned data store and scoped application identity
A query or item access pattern and an explicit retry budget
steps: Create tables, containers or datasets with the intended partitioning.
Grant only the required query or item operations.
Handle throttling, pagination and idempotent writes in the application.
tests: Test representative queries and partition distribution.
Exercise throttling, duplicate delivery and access to a disallowed dataset.
failures: Throttling: inspect partition hotspots, request units or quota.
Missing rows: inspect key selection, consistency and query permissions.

: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_auth_and_tls_enforced_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce TLS Encryption and Require Auth Password on Managed Redis (Tier-7 • Profile S)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.require_ssl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure require_ssl for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application query and data access
developer_guide.contract: Collection or table, partition key, query shape and consistency model
dependencies: A provisioned data store and scoped application identity
A query or item access pattern and an explicit retry budget
steps: Create tables, containers or datasets with the intended partitioning.
Grant only the required query or item operations.
Handle throttling, pagination and idempotent writes in the application.
tests: Test representative queries and partition distribution.
Exercise throttling, duplicate delivery and access to a disallowed dataset.
failures: Throttling: inspect partition hotspots, request units or quota.
Missing rows: inspect key selection, consistency and query permissions.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_disable_dangerous_commands_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Disable Dangerous Redis Commands via Configuration Parameters (Tier-7 • Profile T)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.disabled_commands
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure disabled_commands for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Redis"]
      requirement["Disable Dangerous Redis Commands via Configuration Parameters"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0751"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-redis", label: "Vultr Managed Redis", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

dependencies: A provisioned data store and scoped application identity
A query or item access pattern and an explicit retry budget
steps: Create tables, containers or datasets with the intended partitioning.
Grant only the required query or item operations.
Handle throttling, pagination and idempotent writes in the application.
tests: Test representative queries and partition distribution.
Exercise throttling, duplicate delivery and access to a disallowed dataset.
failures: Throttling: inspect partition hotspots, request units or quota.
Missing rows: inspect key selection, consistency and query permissions.

package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_vpc_only_binding_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Bind Managed Redis Exclusively to VPC 2.0 Internal IP Interfaces (Tier-7 • Profile U)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.vpc2_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc2_id for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application query and data access
developer_guide.contract: Collection or table, partition key, query shape and consistency model
dependencies: A provisioned data store and scoped application identity
A query or item access pattern and an explicit retry budget
steps: Create tables, containers or datasets with the intended partitioning.
Grant only the required query or item operations.
Handle throttling, pagination and idempotent writes in the application.
tests: Test representative queries and partition distribution.
Exercise throttling, duplicate delivery and access to a disallowed dataset.
failures: Throttling: inspect partition hotspots, request units or quota.
Missing rows: inspect key selection, consistency and query permissions.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_auth_and_tls_enforced_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce TLS Encryption and Require Auth Password on Managed Redis (Tier-8 • Profile V)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.require_ssl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure require_ssl for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

steps: Create tables, containers or datasets with the intended partitioning.
Grant only the required query or item operations.
Handle throttling, pagination and idempotent writes in the application.
tests: Test representative queries and partition distribution.
Exercise throttling, duplicate delivery and access to a disallowed dataset.
failures: Throttling: inspect partition hotspots, request units or quota.
Missing rows: inspect key selection, consistency and query permissions.

package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_disable_dangerous_commands_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Disable Dangerous Redis Commands via Configuration Parameters (Tier-8 • Profile W)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.disabled_commands
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure disabled_commands for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application query and data access
developer_guide.contract: Collection or table, partition key, query shape and consistency model
dependencies: A provisioned data store and scoped application identity
A query or item access pattern and an explicit retry budget
steps: Create tables, containers or datasets with the intended partitioning.
Grant only the required query or item operations.
Handle throttling, pagination and idempotent writes in the application.
tests: Test representative queries and partition distribution.
Exercise throttling, duplicate delivery and access to a disallowed dataset.
failures: Throttling: inspect partition hotspots, request units or quota.
Missing rows: inspect key selection, consistency and query permissions.

: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_vpc_only_binding_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Bind Managed Redis Exclusively to VPC 2.0 Internal IP Interfaces (Tier-8 • Profile X)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.vpc2_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc2_id for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application query and data access
developer_guide.contract: Collection or table, partition key, query shape and consistency model
dependencies: A provisioned data store and scoped application identity
A query or item access pattern and an explicit retry budget
steps: Create tables, containers or datasets with the intended partitioning.
Grant only the required query or item operations.
Handle throttling, pagination and idempotent writes in the application.
tests: Test representative queries and partition distribution.
Exercise throttling, duplicate delivery and access to a disallowed dataset.
failures: Throttling: inspect partition hotspots, request units or quota.
Missing rows: inspect key selection, consistency and query permissions.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_auth_and_tls_enforced_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce TLS Encryption and Require Auth Password on Managed Redis (Tier-9 • Profile Y)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.require_ssl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure require_ssl for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Redis"]
      requirement["Enforce TLS Encryption and Require Auth Password on Managed Redis"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0756"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-redis", label: "Vultr Managed Redis", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application query and data access
developer_guide.contract: Collection or table, partition key, query shape and consistency model
dependencies: A provisioned data store and scoped application identity
A query or item access pattern and an explicit retry budget
steps: Create tables, containers or datasets with the intended partitioning.
Grant only the required query or item operations.
Handle throttling, pagination and idempotent writes in the application.
tests: Test representative queries and partition distribution.
Exercise throttling, duplicate delivery and access to a disallowed dataset.
failures: Throttling: inspect partition hotspots, request units or quota.
Missing rows: inspect key selection, consistency and query permissions.

developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_disable_dangerous_commands_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Disable Dangerous Redis Commands via Configuration Parameters (Tier-9 • Profile Z)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.disabled_commands
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure disabled_commands for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application query and data access
developer_guide.contract: Collection or table, partition key, query shape and consistency model
dependencies: A provisioned data store and scoped application identity
A query or item access pattern and an explicit retry budget
steps: Create tables, containers or datasets with the intended partitioning.
Grant only the required query or item operations.
Handle throttling, pagination and idempotent writes in the application.
tests: Test representative queries and partition distribution.
Exercise throttling, duplicate delivery and access to a disallowed dataset.
failures: Throttling: inspect partition hotspots, request units or quota.
Missing rows: inspect key selection, consistency and query permissions.

checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_vpc_only_binding_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Bind Managed Redis Exclusively to VPC 2.0 Internal IP Interfaces (Tier-9 • Profile A)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.vpc2_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc2_id for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application query and data access
developer_guide.contract: Collection or table, partition key, query shape and consistency model
dependencies: A provisioned data store and scoped application identity
A query or item access pattern and an explicit retry budget
steps: Create tables, containers or datasets with the intended partitioning.
Grant only the required query or item operations.
Handle throttling, pagination and idempotent writes in the application.
tests: Test representative queries and partition distribution.
Exercise throttling, duplicate delivery and access to a disallowed dataset.
failures: Throttling: inspect partition hotspots, request units or quota.
Missing rows: inspect key selection, consistency and query permissions.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_auth_and_tls_enforced_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce TLS Encryption and Require Auth Password on Managed Redis (Tier-10 • Profile B)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.require_ssl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure require_ssl for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Redis"]
      requirement["Enforce TLS Encryption and Require Auth Password on Managed Redis"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0759"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-redis", label: "Vultr Managed Redis", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application query and data access
developer_guide.contract: Collection or table, partition key, query shape and consistency model
dependencies: A provisioned data store and scoped application identity
A query or item access pattern and an explicit retry budget
steps: Create tables, containers or datasets with the intended partitioning.
Grant only the required query or item operations.
Handle throttling, pagination and idempotent writes in the application.
tests: Test representative queries and partition distribution.
Exercise throttling, duplicate delivery and access to a disallowed dataset.
failures: Throttling: inspect partition hotspots, request units or quota.
Missing rows: inspect key selection, consistency and query permissions.

: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"

developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_disable_dangerous_commands_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Disable Dangerous Redis Commands via Configuration Parameters (Tier-10 • Profile C)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.disabled_commands
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure disabled_commands for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application query and data access
developer_guide.contract: Collection or table, partition key, query shape and consistency model
dependencies: A provisioned data store and scoped application identity
A query or item access pattern and an explicit retry budget
steps: Create tables, containers or datasets with the intended partitioning.
Grant only the required query or item operations.
Handle throttling, pagination and idempotent writes in the application.
tests: Test representative queries and partition distribution.
Exercise throttling, duplicate delivery and access to a disallowed dataset.
failures: Throttling: inspect partition hotspots, request units or quota.
Missing rows: inspect key selection, consistency and query permissions.

vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_vpc_only_binding_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Bind Managed Redis Exclusively to VPC 2.0 Internal IP Interfaces (Tier-10 • Profile D)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.vpc2_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc2_id for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application query and data access
developer_guide.contract: Collection or table, partition key, query shape and consistency model
dependencies: A provisioned data store and scoped application identity
A query or item access pattern and an explicit retry budget
steps: Create tables, containers or datasets with the intended partitioning.
Grant only the required query or item operations.
Handle throttling, pagination and idempotent writes in the application.
tests: Test representative queries and partition distribution.
Exercise throttling, duplicate delivery and access to a disallowed dataset.
failures: Throttling: inspect partition hotspots, request units or quota.
Missing rows: inspect key selection, consistency and query permissions.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_auth_and_tls_enforced_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce TLS Encryption and Require Auth Password on Managed Redis (Tier-11 • Profile E)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.require_ssl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure require_ssl for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Redis"]
      requirement["Enforce TLS Encryption and Require Auth Password on Managed Redis"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0762"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-redis", label: "Vultr Managed Redis", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application query and data access
developer_guide.contract: Collection or table, partition key, query shape and consistency model
dependencies: A provisioned data store and scoped application identity
A query or item access pattern and an explicit retry budget
steps: Create tables, containers or datasets with the intended partitioning.
Grant only the required query or item operations.
Handle throttling, pagination and idempotent writes in the application.
tests: Test representative queries and partition distribution.
Exercise throttling, duplicate delivery and access to a disallowed dataset.
failures: Throttling: inspect partition hotspots, request units or quota.
Missing rows: inspect key selection, consistency and query permissions.

vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_disable_dangerous_commands_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Disable Dangerous Redis Commands via Configuration Parameters (Tier-11 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.disabled_commands
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure disabled_commands for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application query and data access
developer_guide.contract: Collection or table, partition key, query shape and consistency model
dependencies: A provisioned data store and scoped application identity
A query or item access pattern and an explicit retry budget
steps: Create tables, containers or datasets with the intended partitioning.
Grant only the required query or item operations.
Handle throttling, pagination and idempotent writes in the application.
tests: Test representative queries and partition distribution.
Exercise throttling, duplicate delivery and access to a disallowed dataset.
failures: Throttling: inspect partition hotspots, request units or quota.
Missing rows: inspect key selection, consistency and query permissions.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_vpc_only_binding_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Bind Managed Redis Exclusively to VPC 2.0 Internal IP Interfaces (Tier-11 • Profile G)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.vpc2_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc2_id for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

dependencies: A provisioned data store and scoped application identity
A query or item access pattern and an explicit retry budget
steps: Create tables, containers or datasets with the intended partitioning.
Grant only the required query or item operations.
Handle throttling, pagination and idempotent writes in the application.
tests: Test representative queries and partition distribution.
Exercise throttling, duplicate delivery and access to a disallowed dataset.
failures: Throttling: inspect partition hotspots, request units or quota.
Missing rows: inspect key selection, consistency and query permissions.

package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_auth_and_tls_enforced_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce TLS Encryption and Require Auth Password on Managed Redis (Tier-12 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.require_ssl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure require_ssl for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application query and data access
developer_guide.contract: Collection or table, partition key, query shape and consistency model
dependencies: A provisioned data store and scoped application identity
A query or item access pattern and an explicit retry budget
steps: Create tables, containers or datasets with the intended partitioning.
Grant only the required query or item operations.
Handle throttling, pagination and idempotent writes in the application.
tests: Test representative queries and partition distribution.
Exercise throttling, duplicate delivery and access to a disallowed dataset.
failures: Throttling: inspect partition hotspots, request units or quota.
Missing rows: inspect key selection, consistency and query permissions.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_disable_dangerous_commands_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Disable Dangerous Redis Commands via Configuration Parameters (Tier-12 • Profile I)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.disabled_commands
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure disabled_commands for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application query and data access
developer_guide.contract: Collection or table, partition key, query shape and consistency model
dependencies: A provisioned data store and scoped application identity
A query or item access pattern and an explicit retry budget
steps: Create tables, containers or datasets with the intended partitioning.
Grant only the required query or item operations.
Handle throttling, pagination and idempotent writes in the application.
tests: Test representative queries and partition distribution.
Exercise throttling, duplicate delivery and access to a disallowed dataset.
failures: Throttling: inspect partition hotspots, request units or quota.
Missing rows: inspect key selection, consistency and query permissions.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_vpc_only_binding_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Bind Managed Redis Exclusively to VPC 2.0 Internal IP Interfaces (Tier-12 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.vpc2_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc2_id for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Redis"]
      requirement["Bind Managed Redis Exclusively to VPC 2.0 Internal IP Interfaces"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0767"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-redis", label: "Vultr Managed Redis", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.contract: Collection or table, partition key, query shape and consistency model
dependencies: A provisioned data store and scoped application identity
A query or item access pattern and an explicit retry budget
steps: Create tables, containers or datasets with the intended partitioning.
Grant only the required query or item operations.
Handle throttling, pagination and idempotent writes in the application.
tests: Test representative queries and partition distribution.
Exercise throttling, duplicate delivery and access to a disallowed dataset.
failures: Throttling: inspect partition hotspots, request units or quota.
Missing rows: inspect key selection, consistency and query permissions.

package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_auth_and_tls_enforced_t13

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce TLS Encryption and Require Auth Password on Managed Redis (Tier-13 • Profile K)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.require_ssl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure require_ssl for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application query and data access
developer_guide.contract: Collection or table, partition key, query shape and consistency model
dependencies: A provisioned data store and scoped application identity
A query or item access pattern and an explicit retry budget
steps: Create tables, containers or datasets with the intended partitioning.
Grant only the required query or item operations.
Handle throttling, pagination and idempotent writes in the application.
tests: Test representative queries and partition distribution.
Exercise throttling, duplicate delivery and access to a disallowed dataset.
failures: Throttling: inspect partition hotspots, request units or quota.
Missing rows: inspect key selection, consistency and query permissions.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_disable_dangerous_commands_t13

default allow = false

# Rule: Disable Dangerous Redis Commands via Configuration Parameters (Tier-13 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.disabled_commands
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure disabled_commands for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application query and data access
developer_guide.contract: Collection or table, partition key, query shape and consistency model
dependencies: A provisioned data store and scoped application identity
A query or item access pattern and an explicit retry budget
steps: Create tables, containers or datasets with the intended partitioning.
Grant only the required query or item operations.
Handle throttling, pagination and idempotent writes in the application.
tests: Test representative queries and partition distribution.
Exercise throttling, duplicate delivery and access to a disallowed dataset.
failures: Throttling: inspect partition hotspots, request units or quota.
Missing rows: inspect key selection, consistency and query permissions.

vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_vpc_only_binding_t13

default allow = false

# Rule: Bind Managed Redis Exclusively to VPC 2.0 Internal IP Interfaces (Tier-13 • Profile M)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.vpc2_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc2_id for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Redis"]
      requirement["Bind Managed Redis Exclusively to VPC 2.0 Internal IP Interfaces"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0770"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-redis", label: "Vultr Managed Redis", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.contract: Collection or table, partition key, query shape and consistency model
dependencies: A provisioned data store and scoped application identity
A query or item access pattern and an explicit retry budget
steps: Create tables, containers or datasets with the intended partitioning.
Grant only the required query or item operations.
Handle throttling, pagination and idempotent writes in the application.
tests: Test representative queries and partition distribution.
Exercise throttling, duplicate delivery and access to a disallowed dataset.
failures: Throttling: inspect partition hotspots, request units or quota.
Missing rows: inspect key selection, consistency and query permissions.

package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_auth_and_tls_enforced_t14

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce TLS Encryption and Require Auth Password on Managed Redis (Tier-14 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.require_ssl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure require_ssl for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application query and data access
developer_guide.contract: Collection or table, partition key, query shape and consistency model
dependencies: A provisioned data store and scoped application identity
A query or item access pattern and an explicit retry budget
steps: Create tables, containers or datasets with the intended partitioning.
Grant only the required query or item operations.
Handle throttling, pagination and idempotent writes in the application.
tests: Test representative queries and partition distribution.
Exercise throttling, duplicate delivery and access to a disallowed dataset.
failures: Throttling: inspect partition hotspots, request units or quota.
Missing rows: inspect key selection, consistency and query permissions.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_disable_dangerous_commands_t14

default allow = false

# Rule: Disable Dangerous Redis Commands via Configuration Parameters (Tier-14 • Profile O)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.disabled_commands
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure disabled_commands for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}

steps: Create tables, containers or datasets with the intended partitioning.
Grant only the required query or item operations.
Handle throttling, pagination and idempotent writes in the application.
tests: Test representative queries and partition distribution.
Exercise throttling, duplicate delivery and access to a disallowed dataset.
failures: Throttling: inspect partition hotspots, request units or quota.
Missing rows: inspect key selection, consistency and query permissions.

package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_vpc_only_binding_t14

default allow = false

# Rule: Bind Managed Redis Exclusively to VPC 2.0 Internal IP Interfaces (Tier-14 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.vpc2_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc2_id for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
