developer_guide.name: Application query and data access
developer_guide.contract: Collection or table, partition key, query shape and consistency model
dependencies: A provisioned data store and scoped application identity
A query or item access pattern and an explicit retry budget
steps: Create tables, containers or datasets with the intended partitioning.
Grant only the required query or item operations.
Handle throttling, pagination and idempotent writes in the application.
tests: Test representative queries and partition distribution.
Exercise throttling, duplicate delivery and access to a disallowed dataset.
failures: Throttling: inspect partition hotspots, request units or quota.
Missing rows: inspect key selection, consistency and query permissions.

: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_redis.vultr_redis_redis_auth_and_tls_enforced_t15

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce TLS Encryption and Require Auth Password on Managed Redis (Tier-15 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.require_ssl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure require_ssl for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application query and data access
developer_guide.contract: Collection or table, partition key, query shape and consistency model
dependencies: A provisioned data store and scoped application identity
A query or item access pattern and an explicit retry budget
steps: Create tables, containers or datasets with the intended partitioning.
Grant only the required query or item operations.
Handle throttling, pagination and idempotent writes in the application.
tests: Test representative queries and partition distribution.
Exercise throttling, duplicate delivery and access to a disallowed dataset.
failures: Throttling: inspect partition hotspots, request units or quota.
Missing rows: inspect key selection, consistency and query permissions.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_kafka.vultr_kafka_kafka_sasl_scram_tls_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce SASL/SCRAM Authentication and TLS Encryption on Kafka Brokers
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.kafka_auth_mechanism
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kafka_auth_mechanism for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Kafka"]
      requirement["Enforce SASL/SCRAM Authentication and TLS Encryption on Kafka Brokers"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0775"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-kafka", label: "Vultr Managed Kafka", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_kafka.vultr_kafka_kafka_schema_validation_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Schema Registry Validation to Prevent Malformed Message Ingestion
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.schema_registry_enforced
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure schema_registry_enforced for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify artifact digest, trusted signer identity, and relevant attestations
An image signature establishes provenance only under the configured trust policy. Scan results, deployment admission, and runtime restrictions remain separate controls.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_kafka.vultr_kafka_kafka_private_subnet_restriction_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Isolate Kafka Cluster Within Private Subnet and Restrict Consumer IPs
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.trusted_ips
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure trusted_ips for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Kafka"]
      requirement["Isolate Kafka Cluster Within Private Subnet and Restrict Consumer IPs"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0777"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-kafka", label: "Vultr Managed Kafka", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_kafka.vultr_kafka_kafka_sasl_scram_tls_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce SASL/SCRAM Authentication and TLS Encryption on Kafka Brokers (Tier-2 • Profile D)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.kafka_auth_mechanism
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kafka_auth_mechanism for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_kafka.vultr_kafka_kafka_schema_validation_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Schema Registry Validation to Prevent Malformed Message Ingestion (Tier-2 • Profile E)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.schema_registry_enforced
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure schema_registry_enforced for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Kafka"]
      requirement["Enable Schema Registry Validation to Prevent Malformed Message Ingestion"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0779"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-kafka", label: "Vultr Managed Kafka", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Verify artifact digest, trusted signer identity, and relevant attestations"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify artifact digest, trusted signer identity, and relevant attestations
An image signature establishes provenance only under the configured trust policy. Scan results, deployment admission, and runtime restrictions remain separate controls.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_kafka.vultr_kafka_kafka_private_subnet_restriction_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Isolate Kafka Cluster Within Private Subnet and Restrict Consumer IPs (Tier-2 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.trusted_ips
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure trusted_ips for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_kafka.vultr_kafka_kafka_sasl_scram_tls_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce SASL/SCRAM Authentication and TLS Encryption on Kafka Brokers (Tier-3 • Profile G)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.kafka_auth_mechanism
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kafka_auth_mechanism for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Kafka"]
      requirement["Enforce SASL/SCRAM Authentication and TLS Encryption on Kafka Brokers"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0781"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-kafka", label: "Vultr Managed Kafka", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_kafka.vultr_kafka_kafka_schema_validation_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Schema Registry Validation to Prevent Malformed Message Ingestion (Tier-3 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.schema_registry_enforced
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure schema_registry_enforced for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify artifact digest, trusted signer identity, and relevant attestations
An image signature establishes provenance only under the configured trust policy. Scan results, deployment admission, and runtime restrictions remain separate controls.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_kafka.vultr_kafka_kafka_private_subnet_restriction_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Isolate Kafka Cluster Within Private Subnet and Restrict Consumer IPs (Tier-3 • Profile I)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.trusted_ips
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure trusted_ips for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Kafka"]
      requirement["Isolate Kafka Cluster Within Private Subnet and Restrict Consumer IPs"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0783"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-kafka", label: "Vultr Managed Kafka", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_kafka.vultr_kafka_kafka_sasl_scram_tls_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce SASL/SCRAM Authentication and TLS Encryption on Kafka Brokers (Tier-4 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.kafka_auth_mechanism
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kafka_auth_mechanism for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_kafka.vultr_kafka_kafka_schema_validation_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Schema Registry Validation to Prevent Malformed Message Ingestion (Tier-4 • Profile K)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.schema_registry_enforced
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure schema_registry_enforced for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Kafka"]
      requirement["Enable Schema Registry Validation to Prevent Malformed Message Ingestion"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0785"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-kafka", label: "Vultr Managed Kafka", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Verify artifact digest, trusted signer identity, and relevant attestations"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify artifact digest, trusted signer identity, and relevant attestations
An image signature establishes provenance only under the configured trust policy. Scan results, deployment admission, and runtime restrictions remain separate controls.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_kafka.vultr_kafka_kafka_private_subnet_restriction_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Isolate Kafka Cluster Within Private Subnet and Restrict Consumer IPs (Tier-4 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.trusted_ips
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure trusted_ips for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_kafka.vultr_kafka_kafka_sasl_scram_tls_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce SASL/SCRAM Authentication and TLS Encryption on Kafka Brokers (Tier-5 • Profile M)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.kafka_auth_mechanism
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kafka_auth_mechanism for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Kafka"]
      requirement["Enforce SASL/SCRAM Authentication and TLS Encryption on Kafka Brokers"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0787"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-kafka", label: "Vultr Managed Kafka", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_kafka.vultr_kafka_kafka_schema_validation_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Schema Registry Validation to Prevent Malformed Message Ingestion (Tier-5 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.schema_registry_enforced
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure schema_registry_enforced for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify artifact digest, trusted signer identity, and relevant attestations
An image signature establishes provenance only under the configured trust policy. Scan results, deployment admission, and runtime restrictions remain separate controls.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_kafka.vultr_kafka_kafka_private_subnet_restriction_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Isolate Kafka Cluster Within Private Subnet and Restrict Consumer IPs (Tier-5 • Profile O)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.trusted_ips
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure trusted_ips for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Kafka"]
      requirement["Isolate Kafka Cluster Within Private Subnet and Restrict Consumer IPs"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0789"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-kafka", label: "Vultr Managed Kafka", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_kafka.vultr_kafka_kafka_sasl_scram_tls_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce SASL/SCRAM Authentication and TLS Encryption on Kafka Brokers (Tier-6 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.kafka_auth_mechanism
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kafka_auth_mechanism for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_kafka.vultr_kafka_kafka_schema_validation_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Schema Registry Validation to Prevent Malformed Message Ingestion (Tier-6 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.schema_registry_enforced
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure schema_registry_enforced for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Kafka"]
      requirement["Enable Schema Registry Validation to Prevent Malformed Message Ingestion"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0791"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-kafka", label: "Vultr Managed Kafka", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Verify artifact digest, trusted signer identity, and relevant attestations"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify artifact digest, trusted signer identity, and relevant attestations
An image signature establishes provenance only under the configured trust policy. Scan results, deployment admission, and runtime restrictions remain separate controls.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_kafka.vultr_kafka_kafka_private_subnet_restriction_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Isolate Kafka Cluster Within Private Subnet and Restrict Consumer IPs (Tier-6 • Profile R)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.trusted_ips
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure trusted_ips for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_kafka.vultr_kafka_kafka_sasl_scram_tls_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce SASL/SCRAM Authentication and TLS Encryption on Kafka Brokers (Tier-7 • Profile S)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.kafka_auth_mechanism
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kafka_auth_mechanism for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Kafka"]
      requirement["Enforce SASL/SCRAM Authentication and TLS Encryption on Kafka Brokers"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0793"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-kafka", label: "Vultr Managed Kafka", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_kafka.vultr_kafka_kafka_schema_validation_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Schema Registry Validation to Prevent Malformed Message Ingestion (Tier-7 • Profile T)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.schema_registry_enforced
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure schema_registry_enforced for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify artifact digest, trusted signer identity, and relevant attestations
An image signature establishes provenance only under the configured trust policy. Scan results, deployment admission, and runtime restrictions remain separate controls.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_kafka.vultr_kafka_kafka_private_subnet_restriction_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Isolate Kafka Cluster Within Private Subnet and Restrict Consumer IPs (Tier-7 • Profile U)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.trusted_ips
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure trusted_ips for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Kafka"]
      requirement["Isolate Kafka Cluster Within Private Subnet and Restrict Consumer IPs"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0795"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-kafka", label: "Vultr Managed Kafka", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_kafka.vultr_kafka_kafka_sasl_scram_tls_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce SASL/SCRAM Authentication and TLS Encryption on Kafka Brokers (Tier-8 • Profile V)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.kafka_auth_mechanism
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kafka_auth_mechanism for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_kafka.vultr_kafka_kafka_schema_validation_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Schema Registry Validation to Prevent Malformed Message Ingestion (Tier-8 • Profile W)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.schema_registry_enforced
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure schema_registry_enforced for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Managed Kafka"]
      requirement["Enable Schema Registry Validation to Prevent Malformed Message Ingestion"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0797"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-kafka", label: "Vultr Managed Kafka", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Verify artifact digest, trusted signer identity, and relevant attestations"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify artifact digest, trusted signer identity, and relevant attestations
An image signature establishes provenance only under the configured trust policy. Scan results, deployment admission, and runtime restrictions remain separate controls.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_kafka.vultr_kafka_kafka_private_subnet_restriction_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Isolate Kafka Cluster Within Private Subnet and Restrict Consumer IPs (Tier-8 • Profile X)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_database"
  not r.change.after.trusted_ips
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure trusted_ips for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
