package vultr.vultr_serverless.vultr_serverless_serverless_sandbox_isolation_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Ephemeral Sandbox Isolation on Cloud Inference Workloads (Tier-8 • Profile V)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_inference"
  not r.change.after.sandbox_mode
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure sandbox_mode for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Cloud Inference"]
      requirement["Enforce Ephemeral Sandbox Isolation on Cloud Inference Workloads"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0925"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-serverless", label: "Vultr Cloud Inference", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_serverless.vultr_serverless_serverless_api_quota_limit_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Restrict API Ingress to Token-Authenticated Clients with Strict Quotas (Tier-8 • Profile W)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_inference"
  not r.change.after.rate_limit_per_minute
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure rate_limit_per_minute for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_serverless.vultr_serverless_serverless_model_encryption_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Encrypt In-Flight and Cached Model Artifacts with Customer Keys (Tier-8 • Profile X)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_inference"
  not r.change.after.model_encryption
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure model_encryption for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_serverless.vultr_serverless_serverless_sandbox_isolation_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Ephemeral Sandbox Isolation on Cloud Inference Workloads (Tier-9 • Profile Y)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_inference"
  not r.change.after.sandbox_mode
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure sandbox_mode for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_serverless.vultr_serverless_serverless_api_quota_limit_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Restrict API Ingress to Token-Authenticated Clients with Strict Quotas (Tier-9 • Profile Z)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_inference"
  not r.change.after.rate_limit_per_minute
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure rate_limit_per_minute for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_serverless.vultr_serverless_serverless_model_encryption_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Encrypt In-Flight and Cached Model Artifacts with Customer Keys (Tier-9 • Profile A)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_inference"
  not r.change.after.model_encryption
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure model_encryption for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_serverless.vultr_serverless_serverless_sandbox_isolation_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Ephemeral Sandbox Isolation on Cloud Inference Workloads (Tier-10 • Profile B)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_inference"
  not r.change.after.sandbox_mode
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure sandbox_mode for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_serverless.vultr_serverless_serverless_api_quota_limit_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Restrict API Ingress to Token-Authenticated Clients with Strict Quotas (Tier-10 • Profile C)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_inference"
  not r.change.after.rate_limit_per_minute
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure rate_limit_per_minute for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Cloud Inference"]
      requirement["Restrict API Ingress to Token-Authenticated Clients with Strict Quotas"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0932"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-serverless", label: "Vultr Cloud Inference", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_serverless.vultr_serverless_serverless_model_encryption_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Encrypt In-Flight and Cached Model Artifacts with Customer Keys (Tier-10 • Profile D)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_inference"
  not r.change.after.model_encryption
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure model_encryption for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

# Rule: Enforce Ephemeral Sandbox Isolation on Cloud Inference Workloads (Tier-11 • Profile E)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_inference"
  not r.change.after.sandbox_mode
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure sandbox_mode for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_serverless.vultr_serverless_serverless_api_quota_limit_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Restrict API Ingress to Token-Authenticated Clients with Strict Quotas (Tier-11 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_inference"
  not r.change.after.rate_limit_per_minute
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure rate_limit_per_minute for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Cloud Inference"]
      requirement["Restrict API Ingress to Token-Authenticated Clients with Strict Quotas"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0935"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-serverless", label: "Vultr Cloud Inference", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_serverless.vultr_serverless_serverless_model_encryption_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Encrypt In-Flight and Cached Model Artifacts with Customer Keys (Tier-11 • Profile G)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_inference"
  not r.change.after.model_encryption
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure model_encryption for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_serverless.vultr_serverless_serverless_sandbox_isolation_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Ephemeral Sandbox Isolation on Cloud Inference Workloads (Tier-12 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_inference"
  not r.change.after.sandbox_mode
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure sandbox_mode for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_serverless.vultr_serverless_serverless_api_quota_limit_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Restrict API Ingress to Token-Authenticated Clients with Strict Quotas (Tier-12 • Profile I)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_inference"
  not r.change.after.rate_limit_per_minute
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure rate_limit_per_minute for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Cloud Inference"]
      requirement["Restrict API Ingress to Token-Authenticated Clients with Strict Quotas"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0938"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-serverless", label: "Vultr Cloud Inference", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_serverless.vultr_serverless_serverless_model_encryption_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Encrypt In-Flight and Cached Model Artifacts with Customer Keys (Tier-12 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_inference"
  not r.change.after.model_encryption
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure model_encryption for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_serverless.vultr_serverless_serverless_sandbox_isolation_t13

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Ephemeral Sandbox Isolation on Cloud Inference Workloads (Tier-13 • Profile K)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_inference"
  not r.change.after.sandbox_mode
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure sandbox_mode for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_serverless.vultr_serverless_serverless_api_quota_limit_t13

default allow = false

# Rule: Restrict API Ingress to Token-Authenticated Clients with Strict Quotas (Tier-13 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_inference"
  not r.change.after.rate_limit_per_minute
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure rate_limit_per_minute for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Cloud Inference"]
      requirement["Restrict API Ingress to Token-Authenticated Clients with Strict Quotas"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0941"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-serverless", label: "Vultr Cloud Inference", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_serverless.vultr_serverless_serverless_model_encryption_t13

default allow = false

# Rule: Encrypt In-Flight and Cached Model Artifacts with Customer Keys (Tier-13 • Profile M)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_inference"
  not r.change.after.model_encryption
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure model_encryption for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_serverless.vultr_serverless_serverless_sandbox_isolation_t14

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Ephemeral Sandbox Isolation on Cloud Inference Workloads (Tier-14 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_inference"
  not r.change.after.sandbox_mode
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure sandbox_mode for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_serverless.vultr_serverless_serverless_api_quota_limit_t14

default allow = false

# Rule: Restrict API Ingress to Token-Authenticated Clients with Strict Quotas (Tier-14 • Profile O)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_inference"
  not r.change.after.rate_limit_per_minute
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure rate_limit_per_minute for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"

developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_serverless.vultr_serverless_serverless_model_encryption_t14

default allow = false

# Rule: Encrypt In-Flight and Cached Model Artifacts with Customer Keys (Tier-14 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_inference"
  not r.change.after.model_encryption
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure model_encryption for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_serverless.vultr_serverless_serverless_sandbox_isolation_t15

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Ephemeral Sandbox Isolation on Cloud Inference Workloads (Tier-15 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_inference"
  not r.change.after.sandbox_mode
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure sandbox_mode for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_compliance.vultr_compliance_compliance_cis_benchmark_audit_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Continuous Audit Against CIS Vultr Hardening Guidelines
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_compliance"
  not r.change.after.benchmark
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure benchmark for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

    end

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_compliance.vultr_compliance_compliance_drift_detection_weekly_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Automate Weekly Drift Detection and Alert on Unregistered Public IPs
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_compliance"
  not r.change.after.drift_check_schedule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure drift_check_schedule for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-compliance", label: "Vultr Compliance Posture", h: 64, pos: "b" }

      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_compliance.vultr_compliance_compliance_mandatory_tagging_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Mandatory Resource Tagging for Cost Center and Data Classification
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.tags
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure tags for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_compliance.vultr_compliance_compliance_cis_benchmark_audit_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Continuous Audit Against CIS Vultr Hardening Guidelines (Tier-2 • Profile D)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_compliance"
  not r.change.after.benchmark
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure benchmark for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Compliance Posture"]
      requirement["Enforce Continuous Audit Against CIS Vultr Hardening Guidelines"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0950"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-compliance", label: "Vultr Compliance Posture", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_compliance.vultr_compliance_compliance_drift_detection_weekly_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Automate Weekly Drift Detection and Alert on Unregistered Public IPs (Tier-2 • Profile E)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_compliance"
  not r.change.after.drift_check_schedule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure drift_check_schedule for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.

vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_compliance.vultr_compliance_compliance_mandatory_tagging_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Mandatory Resource Tagging for Cost Center and Data Classification (Tier-2 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.tags
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure tags for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0952"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-compliance", label: "Vultr Compliance Posture", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_compliance.vultr_compliance_compliance_cis_benchmark_audit_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Continuous Audit Against CIS Vultr Hardening Guidelines (Tier-3 • Profile G)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_compliance"
  not r.change.after.benchmark
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure benchmark for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Compliance Posture"]
      requirement["Enforce Continuous Audit Against CIS Vultr Hardening Guidelines"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0953"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-compliance", label: "Vultr Compliance Posture", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package vultr.vultr_compliance.vultr_compliance_compliance_drift_detection_weekly_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Automate Weekly Drift Detection and Alert on Unregistered Public IPs (Tier-3 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_compliance"
  not r.change.after.drift_check_schedule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure drift_check_schedule for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_compliance.vultr_compliance_compliance_mandatory_tagging_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Mandatory Resource Tagging for Cost Center and Data Classification (Tier-3 • Profile I)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_instance"
  not r.change.after.tags
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure tags for compliance standard CIS Vultr Cloud Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Vultr: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Vultr Compliance Posture"]
      requirement["Enforce Mandatory Resource Tagging for Cost Center and Data Classification"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:vultr-iam", label: "Vultr API key or subaccount permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: VULTR-BP-0955"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Vultr: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-compliance", label: "Vultr Compliance Posture", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:vultr-logging", label: "Vultr system audit logs and resource readback", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.

: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package vultr.vultr_compliance.vultr_compliance_compliance_cis_benchmark_audit_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Continuous Audit Against CIS Vultr Hardening Guidelines (Tier-4 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS Vultr Security Guidelines, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "vultr_compliance"
  not r.change.after.benchmark
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure benchmark for compliance standard CIS Vultr Security Guidelines", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Vultr CLI (vultr-cli) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

    end

      resource@{ icon: "logos:vultr-compliance", label: "Vultr Compliance Posture", h: 64, pos: "b" }

      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end
